articles.title: The year Facebook was born, Switzerland hosted its last World Chess Championship; Gukesh vs Sindarov next
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In the early days of social media, racking up a massive friend list was more of a competitive sport for many.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In the early days of social media, racking up a massive friend list was more of a competitive sport for many. A 2008 study by Jolene Zywica and James Danowski found that two-thirds of surveyed people knew someone actively padding their friend count just to look popular, while later research by psychologist Phillip Ozimek showed that materialistic users often collected online friends like digital trophies.Oxford evolutionary psychologist Robin Dunbar, meanwhile, proved that out of hundreds of online connections, only about four actually count as close. But all this came to light because of Facebook, launched by Mark Zuckerberg as TheFacebook in 2004, a year that also gave the world Gmail and saw Google’s landmark initial public offering. But for chess fans, 2004 holds an entirely different resonance.In a corner of southern Switzerland, along the shores of Lake Maggiore in the village of Brissago, Russian Grandmaster Vladimir Kramnik was defending his Classical World Chess Championship crown against Hungarian challenger Peter Leko.For 22 years, Brissago stood as the last time Switzerland hosted a World Chess Championship match.Now, as reigning champion Gukesh Dommaraju prepares to defend his title against Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov on Swiss soil (in Geneva this time), Leko, who will call the action as FIDE’s official commentator alongside Russian Grandmaster Peter Svidler, finds himself looking back at the quiet Alpine lakeside town where he came within a single game of immortality."Switzerland is an amazing place to play a World Championship match because it's very quiet and peaceful," Leko, now 47, recalled during an exclusive interview with TimesofIndia.com. "It lets the players focus fully on the championship without any disruptions. I had a wonderful time in Brissago, so I have very pleasant memories of the organisation and the whole environment."Inside the Centro Dannemann, however, facing Kramnik in 2004 meant stepping into the ring with a champion considered untouchable, a man who had dethroned Garry Kasparov in 2000 without losing a single game."You also have to remember that those were the times before the computer era, before the strong engines," Leko shared with a smile. "Catching up with opening preparation was almost impossible. Kramnik had already played a World Championship match against Kasparov and had been a top-10 player since 1993, when I was still a child. He was way ahead in opening preparation, and that was a big handicap during the match."That preparation gap exploded onto the board immediately. Leko lost the very first game with the white pieces. Under the rules of the era, it looked close to fatal.The 2004 championship was the final title match in history played under the old draw-odds stipulation, meaning if the 14-game contest ended in a 7–7 tie, the title holder would retain the crown.Leko remembers the post-game press conference, where a reporter asked him whether he still believed he had any chance after the opening loss, or why the match was even worth continuing."I became very angry because I felt that there was a reason why I had lost that first game with the white pieces," Leko recalled. "First of all, Kramnik had very good preparation, which was actually based on a queen sacrifice to force a draw and establish a fortress. However, as a young challenger, I felt that the whole world was watching, so I had to keep fighting. I tried to push too hard, and it backfired."Trailing by a full point against an undefeated champion with an extra white game still to come, Leko realised that survival depended on leaning completely on his seconds. But how did he do that?"That is a very good question," he smiled again. "I realised that I had to forget about what people were thinking or saying. I had to focus only on myself, my game, and my team. That was absolutely the right decision. I completely shut myself off from outside noise and expectations. I just wanted to prove to myself that I had a chance."Leko, with white pieces, had spent months preparing to dismantle Kramnik’s famed Berlin Defence against 1.e4.But in the match, Kramnik ambushed him with an airtight Petroff Defence that neutralised everything Leko had built. Over the next three games, draws dominated the scene.In Game 5, Leko abandoned his primary weapon altogether and opened with 1.d4, stepping straight into Kramnik’s own signature territory."Even today, with computers, it's difficult to switch from 1.e4 to 1.d4," Leko said. "But more than 20 years ago, when experience and time mattered so much, it was a huge challenge to transfer my game to 1.d4 during the match. I managed to win the fifth game with my 1.d4 and tie the match. That was like a miracle. After that, I knew I would have all the chances. My advantage was that he didn't know how much I knew."Leko surged ahead in Game 8 with a celebrated victory using the Marshall Attack with Black and entered the 14th and final game needing only a draw to become World Champion.Kramnik, cornered and desperate, conjured a masterpiece in the final round to level the score at 7–7 and retain his title on the draw rule."Of course, when I lost the last game and the match ended 7–7, it felt like a big tragedy," Leko reminisced."It hurt very much because I was so close to becoming World Champion. But looking back, I'm extremely proud to have had the chance to play that match with Kramnik and make it 7–7, because Kramnik was considered invincible in those days."Two decades later, Leko sees those exact psychological currents, mostly hype, hidden preparation, and the weight of expectation, shaping the Gukesh–Sindarov showdown in Switzerland.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: KC Current Beat Washington Spirit to Win Historic NWSL Championship, Top Highlights and Photos
articles.summary: The Kansas City Current are NWSL champions.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Current are NWSL champions.

Vanessa DiBernardo and Debinha scored in a 2-1 victory over Trinity Rodman and the Washington Spirit Saturday night at Audi Field in Washington, D.C to capture the franchise's first-ever title.

Rodman looked shaken up after colliding with Laney Rouse early before returning to the competition.

That set the tone for a physical first half that set a NWSL championship game record with 19 fouls, per the Beaver County Times ' Rachael Palmer .

DiBernardo broke through when she scored an oOimpico on a corner kick early in the second half to open KC's championship account.

The Spirit's Esme Morgan came close to scoring an equalizer on a corner kick of her own in the 75th minute but couldn't get past a diving save from Current goalkeeper Lorena.

Rodman was involved in another collision late in the game, this time involving Lorena. Both players initially went down but stayed in the game.

The title tilt heated up in stoppage time. Debinha started out by adding some insurance for the Current when the NWSL's all-time leading goalscorer scored on a breakaway.

Rodman quickly answered by heading in the Spirit's first goal of the game, but she was unable to complete the comeback before time expired.

The Current were the first team in NWSL history to enter a playoff game on a seven-game winning streak.

Their eighth straight victory meant heartbreak for Rodman and the Spirit, who have made three consecutive championships only to lose by one goal each time.

articles.title: Florida escapes against Vanderbilt courtesy of lucky bounce in another close SEC finish
articles.summary: Aaron Philo piled up 314 total yards and two touchdowns as Jon Sumrall's Florida Gators rallied late to edge Vanderbilt in a wild SEC finish.
articles.body: Florida’s 2026 season has been defined by highs and lows, and Week 12 delivered one of the Gators’ high points. It took a late rally and a fortunate bounce, but in the end, Florida celebrated a 34-27 victory in front of more than 88,000 fans at The Swamp. Florida quarterback Aaron Philo accounted for 314 yards and two touchdowns, while running back Jadan Baugh scored with just over two minutes left on the clock to complete the latest chapter in the Gators' up-and-down year. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "I’ll take all the luck we can get," Florida head coach Jon Sumrall said. "We need it right now. We need all of it. I’m never going to be above taking luck." Gators wide receiver Eric Singleton Jr. chipped in a career-high 117 yards receiving and had the play of the game. Philo threw high to Micah Mays on third-and-5 in the fourth quarter, but the ball ricocheted into Singleton’s hands for a 37-yard gain. A roughing-the-passer penalty set Baugh up for his 16th touchdown of the season, a 10-yard scamper from the wildcat formation. FLORIDA GATORS MAY OR MAY NOT BE ‘BACK,’ BUT ONE THING IS CERTAIN, FOOTBALL IS FINALLY FUN IN THE SWAMP AGAIN "I didn’t know it was tipped," Philo, who was on the ground as the play unfolded, said. "I really didn’t know it was happening. But I’m glad it happened." Vanderbilt has now dropped seven of their past eight games and will miss a bowl game for the first time since 2023. "We left too many plays on the field to beat a team that found a way in the critical moments to move the ball and score and to generate stops," Vandy coach Clark Lea said. Commodores quarterback Jared Curtis threw two touchdown passes in the second quarter, including a 75-yarder to Junior Sherrill, to put Vanderbilt ahead 24-17 at halftime and draw a chorus of boos from the home team. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Saturday’s win marked the first time since late September that Florida had won consecutive games. The Gators also finished SEC play with a winning record for the first time since 2020. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Gukesh has the crown, Sindarov has the momentum: A clash of two journeys
articles.summary: KOLKATA: As a child, Gukesh Dommaraju would often scribble on the walls of his room.
articles.body: KOLKATA: As a child, Gukesh Dommaraju would often scribble on the walls of his room. His wish was simple: “I want to be the youngest world champion.” At 18, he turned that childhood dream into reality, beating China’s Ding Liren in the World Chess Championship final in Singapore in 2024.Two years on, 20-year-old Gukesh faces a very different challenge. Having gone from being a young challenger taking on a vastly more experienced opponent to a reigning champion defending his crown, he must now contend with a rival his own age — Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov — in the 2026 World Chess Championship final in Geneva, Switzerland, from Tuesday onwards.The past two years have taken the world’s fourthyoungest (Gukesh) and sixth-youngest (Sindarov) Grandmasters in opposite directions. Gukesh has struggled to build on his World Championship triumph and is yet to win a tournament since that victory, while his rating has slipped from 2794 in Oct 2024 to 2703 in Sept 2026. Sindarov, by contrast, has surged, winning the 2025 World Cup and the 2026 Candidates Tournament to reach career-best marks in both rating and world ranking.When Gukesh challenged Ding in 2024, he was rated 55 points higher than the defending champion. This time, he starts as the lowest-ranked reigning champ in World Championship history at World No. 26. Sindarov, meanwhile, enjoys a 72-point rating advantage and a 22-place lead in the Nov FIDE rankings.The Uzbek’s coach, too, has noticed a change in his ward’s demeanour. Roman Vidonyak now describes Sindarov as a “predator”, suggesting that he is increasingly turning into a hunter on the board.Yet Gukesh’s recent slump appears less about his chess than about handling the weight of the title. He showed remarkable composure at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand this year, willingly dropping to Board 4. Still, costly slips from advantageous positions — against Nodirbek Abdusattorov at the Prague Masters; and Arjun Erigaisi and M Pranesh at the Chennai Grand Masters — have exposed Gukesh’ recent vulnerabilities.Hogging the limelight so young carries its own burden, and the pressure has begun to tell. “Obviously there’s a lot of pressure, that I’m dealing with and I’ve not found the right way to maybe handle it yet,” Gukesh had admitted in a recent interaction.Playing away from home in Geneva could offer a welcome buffer from the outside noise and allow Gukesh to rediscover the freedom with which he played his way to the world title in 2024.One-time reigning champ vs first-time challengerlTigran Petrosian vs Boris Spassky (1966): Petrosian (age: 36) edged fellow Soviet GM Spassky (29) 12.5–11.5 to keep the crown.lDing Liren vs D Gukesh (2024): Indian challenger Gukesh (18) upset Chinese GM Ding (32) 7.5–6.5.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Five quick takeaways from Las Vegas GP
articles.summary: Max Verstappen wins Las Vegas drag race
articles.body:
In America's artificial entertainment capital, F1 put the most artificial and entertaining spectacle. How fitting.

The yo-yo racing from the early days of the 2026 season was back on full display, with the lack of electric energy available on the Strip's mile long straight bring back battery driven overtaking. For a while it felt like we were watching the Indy 500, with the top cars trading the lead without being able to break away from the rest of the pack.

It led to numerous position changes and plenty of wheel-to-wheel races, much to the delight of the soldout crowd and event officials.

It's certainly not for everyone, but you can't deny there was something to watch. And it was certainly a much better watch than the Madring's Spanish Grand Prix.

Ferrari in meltdown as Hamilton and Leclerc clash again

Ferrari came into Las Vegas with two clear objectives: Try to win (naturally) and try to lockdown second place in the F1 world constructors' championship. While the first target was going to be a tall order given the Scuderia's lack of engine punch on the long Las Vegas straights, not losing more than 10 points to Red Bull was entirely realistic to second P2.

But then the unsolved objectives reared up once again.

Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc seem unable to race each other as team-mates. That much was evident in Mexico as they cost each other the win, but clear-the-air talks were meant to have solved all that in Brazil. Two weeks later, it is worse than ever.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari

Hamilton vented his fury at Leclerc for fighting him in the pack during the opening act of the Las Vegas GP slipstreaming, battery-boosting 'race', with the Monegasque on the scene when he ran off the road and kept ahead of Lando Norris to pick up a 10-second penalty.

After having to serve his penalty a lap into the safety car period, in order not to hold up Leclerc who was behind him, the pair re-engaged their on-track disagreements and it was Leclerc's turn to make the error. But this time he clattered into his team-mate, spinning Hamilton around, and earning himself a 10s penalty. Whatever was said in Brazil clearly went in one ear and out of the other.

An old rivalry was reignited in Las Vegas this weekend following an incident during FP3, the session that usually generates the fewest headlines over a Grand Prix weekend. Verstappen and Russell went wheel-to-wheel as if they were fighting for position in a race, and the Briton didn't hold back when speaking to the media afterwards, claiming that his rival "thinks he is more important than everyone else" and that "someone needs to put him in his place".

There was a mixture of rivalry and psychological gamesmanship at play, with the two drivers also fighting for second place in the drivers' championship. However, beating Verstappen at mind games is almost as difficult as beating him on track, and the Dutchman barely reacted to Russell's comments.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes

Starting first and second, there was no drama between them at the start of the race, but the pair went on to exchange the lead several times in a series of overtakes. In the end, Verstappen always seemed to have the situation under control: every time Russell managed to get past him, the Dutchman hit back, showing that the verbal attacks from the previous day hadn't affected him in the slightest.

Ultimately, Russell lost out and finished well outside the podium places, while Verstappen went on to win the race and move ever closer to securing second place in the championship.

When word started spreading through the paddock around the Monaco Grand Prix that the FIA had decided Red Bull had a benchmark power unit in F1 in 2026, many thought it was just a bad joke. Red Bull wasn't even close to challenging for wins at the start of the championship, and the verdict sounded almost laughable.

Yet perhaps the engine wasn't really what was holding the Milton Keynes team back, but the car itself. That car is now largely sorted, and Max Verstappen is consistently fighting at the front. And the Las Vegas Grand Prix, with Verstappen and Isack Hadjar battling Mercedes on equal terms, perhaps confirms that the FIA's measurements weren't too far off in the first place.

Pierre Gasly has made something of a speciality of Las Vegas since its arrival on the calendar in 2023. Twice he has qualified on the second row, and even last year, in an Alpine usually consigned to the back of the field, he reached Q3. Yet until this weekend, he had never scored a point there.

His pace was evident again this time. Gasly was second in the wet in FP2 and impressed again in Q2, although ninth in Q3 left him feeling he had missed an opportunity.

The race finally brought the reward his speed around the Strip had long promised. Gasly made early progress and spent much of the grand prix in contention for a podium. That challenge faded with 15 laps to go, but fifth place was a deserved return.

With Alpine having scored just one point across the previous six grands prix, Gasly's result, backed up by sixth for Franco Colapinto, was exactly what the team needed. The double retirement for Racing Bulls allowed Alpine to claw back some ground in the fight for fifth, although catching its rival over the final two rounds still looks a tall order.

Much of Alpine's pace was probably down to the circuit's characteristics. There are some parallels with Monza, where Gasly claimed a surprise pole in September, but Qatar could also suit the A526 as the team bids to finish the season on a stronger note.

articles.title: Kansas City Current defeat Washington Spirit 2-1 to lift first NWSL title
articles.summary: Trinity Rodman left in tears after scoring Spirit’s only goal as DiBernardo and Debinha give Current a closely fought win.
articles.body:
Kansas City Current have defeated the Washington Spirit in a closely-contested final to be crowned the NWSL champions for the first time as Trinity Rodman’s bid to avoid a third consecutive final defeat ended in bitter disappointment in Washington, DC.

Vanessa DiBernardo curled in a goal direct from a corner and Brazilian international Debinha added a second in stoppage time to set up Kansas City’s 2-1 victory at Audi Field on Saturday.

Rodman headed in a 98th-minute goal to pull one back for Spirit, but Kansas City held on to win.

“We knew it was going to be a battle; we felt good coming out of the first half,” said DiBernardo, who was named the championship MVP months after returning to professional football following the birth of her daughter.

“We just had to be patient and finish off the game.”

It was another crushing loss for United States star Rodman and her Spirit teammates, who were also beaten in the final in 2025 and 2024.

Rodman, who was in tears at the final whistle, was knocked out of her stride earlier in the game.

The 24-year-old was on the receiving end of a rugged aerial challenge from Kansas City’s Laney Rouse after just five minutes and needed treatment on the sidelines.

Rodman returned to the field grimacing in pain and clutching her shoulder but completed the game.

The opening goal came early in the second half, with DiBernardo’s in-swinging corner looping into the net after Kansas City’s Kayla Sharples cleverly blocked Washington goalkeeper Sandy MacIver.

Deep in stoppage time, Debinha added Current’s second after a sweeping counterattack, before Rodman’s header was too little, too late.

The victory was Kansas City’s first NWSL title after losing in the championship game to the Portland Thorns in 2022.

articles.title: Wembanyama scores 50 points, bags 19 rebounds in Spurs’ 14th win of season
articles.summary: Wembanyama was just shy of his career-high score of 52 points, set in a victory over Dallas on November 4.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama has scored 50 points and grabbed 19 rebounds to power San Antonio to a 114-91 victory over New Orleans as the Spurs matched the National Basketball Association’s best record at 14-3.

The 22-year-old, 7-foot-4-inch (2.24m) Frenchman made 20 of 29 shots from the floor, 5 of 11 from three-point range, and added five blocked shots, four steals and an assist in 32 minutes on the court on Saturday.

San Antonio won for the 14th time in 15 games, and Wembanyama became only the third NBA player since the 1973-74 season with at least 50 points, 15 rebounds, four steals and five blocks in a game.

“It is very special, but unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat-padding,” Wembanyama said.

Wembanyama was just shy of his career-high score of 52 points , set in a victory over Dallas on November 4.

“Wemby” scored 17 points in the first quarter as the Spurs jumped to a 32-29 lead over the visiting Pelicans and had 32 points and 13 rebounds at half-time with San Antonio ahead 61-45.

“I thought he started the game off aggressive, and I thought he was trying to play with a lot of force offensively, specifically, just in terms of taking up real estate, trying to get to the rim,” Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said.

“I thought he did a really good job of playing with force.”

Johnson did not relish taking Wemby to the bench but wanted to avoid any chance of an injury in a game well in hand.

“Was it tough to pull him out after he got 50? No, I was just hoping he got to 50 when he did,” Johnson said. “That would have been hard to take him out that close to 50.”

The Spurs levelled with the Los Angeles Lakers and Philadelphia 76ers for the best record in the league, the Sixers having matched the mark earlier in a 132-129 victory over Milwaukee.

Joel Embiid led the Philadelphia 76ers to a fifth consecutive victory despite Tyler Herro’s career-high 50 points for the Bucks.

Embiid delivered 26 points, a season-high 17 rebounds and nine assists for the host Sixers as they dropped the league-worst Bucks to 1-16, stretching Milwaukee’s losing skid to 13 games.

Herro added 11 rebounds and seven assists, but he missed a chance to send the game into overtime.

He sank a three-point shot at the finish, but officials ruled after consulting video replay that the shot left his hand after the final buzzer.

Four-time NBA Most Valuable Player LeBron James scored 21 points, grabbed six rebounds, recorded three steals and provided six assists for the 76ers.

“For us to be a super complete team, I think the power of the pass is very infectious,” James said. “It’s key for our other guys as well to make sure they feel in a rhythm and they feel confident.”

Anfernee Simons added 18 points off the Philadelphia bench while Tyrese Maxey added 17 and VJ Edgecombe scored 16 as the 76ers withstood a late Bucks rally.

“Soon we’re going to have to put together a 48-minute game,” Maxey said.

At Madison Square Garden, Mikal Bridges sank a three-pointer at the final buzzer to give the reigning champions New York Knicks a 97-96 victory over Portland.

The Trail Blazers rallied from a 26-point deficit to seize a 96-94 lead on two free throws by Deni Avdija with 3.2 seconds remaining.

The Knicks tried to inbound the ball to star Jalen Brunson for the last shot but went to Bridges when Brunson was covered.

“They played harder than us in that second half,” Bridges said. “That’s on us, but we just finished the game. It goes 48 minutes, and we just kept persevering through the time and ended up winning.”

The Knicks, without injured starters OG Anunoby and Karl-Anthony Towns, improved to 10-6 with their fourth consecutive victory while Portland fell to 10-6.

Brunson led New York with 30 points, 19 of them in the first quarter, while Landry Shamet added 20 and Bridges had 12 points.

In other games, Jaden McDaniels scored 25 points to lead Minnesota’s 104-95 home win over Memphis, while Kyrie Irving had 25 points and Cooper Flagg added 22 in a 110-100 Dallas home win over the Los Angeles Clippers.

articles.title: Max Verstappen wins F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix for third time in four years
articles.summary: Red Bull’s Verstappen dug deep to fend off Antonelli and Russell in a race that saw a jaw-dropping 35 lead changes.
articles.body:
Red Bull’s Max Verstappen won a crazy, slipstreaming Las Vegas Grand Prix for the third time in four years, while Mercedes rival George Russell hit the barriers late on and finished ⁠ninth.

In a race featuring 35 lead changes over 50 laps, with drivers running nose-to-tail under the floodlights and track advantage swinging back and forth like a yo-yo, McLaren’s 2025 champion Lando Norris and teammate Oscar Piastri finished second and third behind the pole-sitter on Saturday.

Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collided again in a ‌race in which both collected 10-second penalties for separate incidents and finished seventh and 10th, respectively.

“That was crazy. Really, really surreal and something I’ve never seen before in Formula One myself,” said Verstappen, who beat Norris by 0.639 seconds.

“It was a crazy amount of fighting, and the slipstream was so big that it was just impossible to drive off and it was just crazy how many people were just following.”

Mercedes have already won both titles , with 20-year-old Italian ⁠Kimi Antonelli this month becoming the youngest ever Formula One world champion , ⁠while Verstappen and Russell started the weekend scrapping to end the season as overall runner-up.

Verstappen’s fourth win in six races sent him 37 points clear of Ferrari’s Hamilton, with Russell, who started on the front row, dropping to fourth overall and ⁠level with Norris.

Antonelli was fourth, with Alpine’s Pierre Gasly fifth and teammate Franco Colapinto sixth. Carlos Sainz was eighth for Williams in the Spaniard’s ⁠250th race.

“I think that must have been the most chaotic ⁠race ever in the history of Formula One,” said Norris.

“I didn’t know what was happening half the time. I didn’t know if I was going to have the best race and have a chance to win or end up last. It had ‌everything this race.”

Piastri, who started 17th, could only agree.

“They say Las Vegas is the entertainment capital of the world and that was pretty entertaining to be a part of,” said the Australian.

“It was ‌pretty ‌random. You would pass someone on one straight super easy, then the next straight you would struggle and then with someone else it would be different strengths and weaknesses.”

articles.title: Gukesh vs Sindarov: The youngest World Chess Championship in history
articles.summary: India’s Gukesh defends his title against Uzbekistan’s Sindarov in up to 14 games in Geneva from November 22.
articles.body:
India’s Gukesh Dommaraju will defend his world chess title against Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva, Switzerland, from November 22 to December 12.

The match, at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny on the outskirts of Geneva, will be played over a maximum of 14 classical games. The first player to reach 7½ points will be crowned world champion.

Both players will be 20 when the first game begins on November 24, making it the youngest world championship match in history.

The official programme opens with a media day and opening ceremony on November 22. The first game is on November 24, and the 14th and final classical game is scheduled for December 11.

A win earns one point, a draw half a point and a loss none. Players have 120 minutes for their first 40 moves, then 30 minutes for the rest of the game, with 30 seconds added per move from move 41. Draw offers are not allowed before move 40.

If the score is tied at 7–7 after 14 games, the title will be decided on December 12 through tiebreaks at faster time controls, starting with four rapid games.

The players will share a $2.5m prize fund. Each earns $200,000 per game won, and the rest is split equally.

Gukesh made history in December 2024, when he defeated China’s Ding Liren in Singapore to become the youngest undisputed world champion, aged 18. Geneva will be his first title defence.

Sindarov won the 2025 FIDE World Cup, then the 2026 Candidates Tournament in Cyprus, where he went unbeaten and scored 10 points from 14 games. Victory in Geneva would make him the first undisputed world champion from Uzbekistan. His compatriot Rustam Kasimdzhanov won FIDE’s version of the title in 2004, when the crown was split.

Sindarov arrives with the stronger record against his opponent. He leads their classical head-to-head 2–0 with one draw, and Gukesh has never beaten him in a classical game.

Since Wilhelm Steinitz became the first recognised world chess champion in 1886, 21 players have held the title over 140 years.

The championship’s history reflects the changing balance of power in chess. European masters dominated its early decades, with Germany’s Emanuel Lasker holding the title for a record 27 years, from 1894 to 1921.

After the second world war, Soviet players took over. From 1948 until 1972, every world champion came from the Soviet Union, beginning with Mikhail Botvinnik.

That run ended in 1972, when American Bobby Fischer defeated Boris Spassky in a match that became a defining moment of the Cold War. The title returned to Soviet hands in 1975, starting the era of Anatoly Karpov and Garry Kasparov, whose rivalry shaped chess for the next two decades.

In 1993, Kasparov broke away from FIDE, chess’s governing body, to form the Professional Chess Association. Two rival world titles existed until they were reunified in 2006. Since then, the crown has passed to India’s Viswanathan Anand, Norway’s Magnus Carlsen, China’s Ding Liren and, in 2024, Gukesh Dommaraju.

The Soviet Union and Russia have produced nine of the 22 champions. India has produced two, Anand and Gukesh, and 11 other countries have each produced one.

In Geneva, either Gukesh will join the small group of players who have defended the title, or Sindarov will add Uzbekistan’s name to the list of undisputed champions.

articles.title: Iraqi bodybuilding champion Sajad Jawad dies days after winning the Asian crown
articles.summary: Sajad Jawad died three days after winning the gold medal in the 90kg category at the Asian Championships in Thailand.
articles.body:
Sports fans in Iraq are mourning the death of international bodybuilding champion Sajad Jawad, who died aged 30 three days after winning a gold medal at the Asian Championships in Thailand.

Jawad’s death was announced by Iraq’s Bodybuilding and Fitness Federation (IBFF) on Thursday, Iraqi media reports said.

“Iraqi international bodybuilding champion Sajjad Jawad has passed away,” the Iraqi News Agency reported, citing an IBFF statement.

“IBFF Iraq’s president, Faiz Abdul Hassan, and its members extend their deepest condolences to the late champion’s family and loved ones,” the statement added, without elaborating on the nature or manner of his death.

Jawad’s gold medal at the recent championships was widely celebrated in the country after he had previously finished 11th in the 90kg category at the same event.

He represented Iraq at several continental and national competitions in his short-lived career, according to reports in national media.

The comments on Jawad’s last social media post, published shortly after his win, run into the hundreds, with fans expressing their shock at his death.

“My heart is broken at this news,” Haider Waleed, a social media user, commented, while others pointed out how a national celebration turned into sorrow within days.

articles.title: Messi throws ball in opponent’s face, avoids red card as Inter Miami lose
articles.summary: Lionel Messi escapes red-card booking for controversial throw-in in Miami’s 3-0 defeat by Columbus in MLS Cup playoffs.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi is at the centre of a controversy after hurling the ball at an opponent during a throw-in and after the Columbus Crew coach says the Inter Miami superstar should have been sent off instead of receiving a yellow card.

The incident took place on Saturday during Miami’s 3-0 home defeat by Columbus in the first game of a best-of-three series in the MLS Cup playoffs.

With 10-man Miami 1-0 down at the stroke of half-time, Messi’s frustration boiled over as he aimed a forceful throw-in into the face of Columbus Crew forward Gonzalo Tapia.

Tapia, less than a metre (3ft) away and trying to impede Messi’s actions, threw himself to the ground after the ball hit his face while Messi appealed for a handball.

Referee Allen Chapman showed yellow cards to both Messi and Tapia, but coach Laurent Courtois said afterwards Messi should have been given a red card.

“Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card,” Courtois said in a postgame news conference when asked about the incident.

What are the laws and rules about Messi’s actions at the throw-in?

According to the International Football Association Board Law 12 , which pertains to fouls and misconduct, the appropriate disciplinary action for such an incident would be both players being “cautioned (yellow card) for unsporting behaviour”.

It adds that the player taking the throw-in could be “sent off (red card) for violent conduct (if the thrower used excessive force)”.

Chapman defended his decision to brandish a yellow card to Messi.

“The force used was negligible, and the offence did not reach the level of violent conduct,” the referee told a pool reporter.

Tapia, who scored twice for Columbus in the win, refrained from commenting on the referee’s decision, saying, “I don’t know if it’s a red card, but I am not the referee to say. It stays there.”

Miami head coach Kily Gonzalez also echoed Tapia’s thoughts, adding that the “card doesn’t change much”.

“The referee saw a yellow, and that is it. We can’t blame the referee,” Gonzalez told reporters. “Sometimes they make mistakes. Sometimes they don’t like each one of us, and we have to accept it.”

The 3-0 defeat means seventh-seeded Columbus, the 2023 champions, could eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in game two of the series in Ohio on Friday.

“It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them,” Gonzalez said.

“We didn’t produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don’t win, we’re out,” he added.

Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi, second from right, argues with Columbus Crew forward Gonzalo Tapia after Messi and Tapia received yellow cards [David Santiago-Imagn Images]

articles.title: Is WWE or AEW Having a Better 2026?
articles.summary: With 2026 having been nothing short of newsworthy for both WWE and AEW, it hasn't been uncommon for the pendulum of momentum to swing back and forth between the two promotions throughout the year.
articles.body:
With 2026 having been nothing short of newsworthy for both WWE and AEW, it hasn't been uncommon for the pendulum of momentum to swing back and forth between the two promotions throughout the year.

The quality of the creative direction has been a primary point of contention among fans, especially in regards to WWE. They haven't had John Cena's farewell tour or nearly as many notable names to fall back on this year, forcing management to make new stars and elevate certain competitors to greater success.

The same can be said for AEW, as a handful of fresh faces have risen up over the last year and are well on their way to winning world titles. AEW has always prided itself on being where the best wrestle, but some of the stories they've told this year with their top talent put their product at a level above WWE's more often than not.

AEW hasn't been without its flaws, however, as depth in the women's division outside of the top title picture has been a recurring issue in the absence of Toni Storm. WWE has experienced similar struggles with Rhea Ripley, Bianca Belair and Asuka missing most of the year for various reasons.

There has been a lot to like about both WWE and AEW as well as much that's been criticized, but which company has had the better 2026 on the whole?

The Highs and Lows of the Men's Main Event Scenes

The men's world title scenes have largely carried WWE and AEW at different points in 2026 and arguably have been the most must-see aspects of both products.

CM Punk was a fighting World Heavyweight champion up until he lost the title to Roman Reigns in an instant classic on Night 2 of WrestleMania 42. Although Reigns hasn't been around remotely as much, he has delivered big time whenever the gold has been up for grabs and might be in the midst of his best in-ring year ever.

The Undisputed WWE Championship picture wasn't quite as consistent for the first half of the year, but Punk taking the title from Zayn in July followed by Zayn getting the belt back in September injected excitement into the top of the card on SmackDown and has made for an unpredictable period where almost anyone has been able to challenge for the championship at any time.

The scene surrounding the AEW World Championship has been slightly stronger in 2026, if only because of how many people were vying for the prestigious prize between January and August. MJF did an outstanding job of holding down the fort as the champ as well as Darby Allin during the thrilling one month that he held it for.

Ospreay is approaching the three-month mark with the AEW World title and is still finding his footing in the role, but at least he has no shortage of credible contenders waiting in the wings with MJF next up for an opportunity.

Despite the three men's world championships across WWE and AEW feeling more important than they have in some time in 2026, there has been an overall lack of long-term stories that have stood out in both companies, including outside of the main event scene.

Only a few feuds have spawned multiple months, and they haven't necessarily been riveting. Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton started out extremely disappointing and did improve once Pat McAfee was removed from the equation, but it felt like the damage had been done, and Rhodes' waning crowd support hasn't helped matters.

WWE's sole overarching story this year has been with The Bloodline, an angle that has been done to death since it started in 2020. Their ongoing war with The 946 has been a recurring highlight on Raw since SummerSlam and justifies the WarGames stipulation at Survivor Series, but there's been very little long-term direction otherwise.

Similar to WWE, AEW has excelled with making moments in 2026 and sending the message that anything can happen on the weekly television shows, but virtually none of their feuds will go down as being their best ever once this year is over.

Will Ospreay, MJF, Darby Allin and Kenny Omega all made magic on and off throughout the year, and the AEW World Championship scene in general was brilliantly booked from the beginning of 2026 through August's All In event, but the product hasn't been nearly as hot in the months due to most matches coming together on the fly instead of telling stories that extend beyond one event.

If anything, The Bloodline have been more of a sure thing this year than anything else in wrestling and that storyline has somehow exceeded expectations, but even that required WWE to bring back a group that was well past its peak in order to get viewers invested again.

The Next Generation Is Gradually Taking Over

Of course, WWE can't rely on The Bloodline forever, and already it's evident that they aren't generating the same success they once did. That's why it's important to use something as established as that faction to elevate the talent of tomorrow, most notably Oba Femi.

Although his absence from either world championship picture has been inexcusable, Femi has been the best call-up from NXT in years. He beat Brock Lesnar in his retirement match at SummerSlam and is the obvious choice to dethrone Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship at WrestleMania 43.

Trick Williams and Je'Von Evans, who were also called up to the main roster this year, have gotten over with the audience and have done extremely well for themselves. WWE hasn't put that same amount of effort into the women they've brought up from NXT (more on that later), but at least there's more variety than there's been before.

Likewise, AEW won't always have Will Ospreay, Kenny Omega, MJF and others in prominent positions due to age, injuries and the very real possibility of any of them (specifically MJF) making the jump to WWE. Thus, they've taken the necessary steps to spotlighting the up-and-coming likes of Kevin Knight, Thekla, Maya World, Kyle Fletcher and others.

Even Andrade El Idolo, Tommaso Ciampa, The New Level, Royce Keys and Danhausen have benefited from swapping promotions in 2026. WWE and AEW's rosters are stacked with stars, but it's up to the respective creative teams to do right by them and utilize them to their full potential.

AEW's Pay-Per-View Quality Has Been Unmatched

AEW has been producing pay-per-views of an exceptional quality since the inception of the promotion, but the run they've been on in 2026 alone has been almost untouchable.

There hasn't been a bad one in the bunch, as even when the pay-per-view builds have been lacking, AEW has shown out with all of their events by maximizing every minute they have available to them.

Revolution, Dynasty and Double or Nothing improved upon each other, followed by a fun Forbidden Door and a rock-solid (albeit unnecessary) Redemption show. Meanwhile, All In 2026 was the greatest installment of the event yet, and the three shows since then (All Out, WrestleDream and Full Gear) have been loaded with stellar wrestling.

WWE has had the exact opposite trend with their premium live events this year in that none of them have truly felt special or worth rewatching after the fact. Royal Rumble and Elimination Chamber were both dull, WrestleMania 42 was infamously a mixed bag, and Clash in Italy and Night of Champions were fine yet forgettable.

SummerSlam was an enjoyable event and both Backlash and Money in the Bank had their fair share of highlights, but WWE's subpar creative in 2026 has prevented them from going all out with their events and emphasizing the action as much as they do the sponsorships, celebrity cameos and commercialization of the product.

This Is The Least Interesting WWE's Women's Division Has Been in Years

As previously noted, WWE has a stronger women's division now than at any other point in the promotion's history, yet the booking of the divisions on Raw and SmackDown hasn't been this abysmal and uninspired in a decade or longer.

Jade Cargill barely defended her WWE Women's Championship in the first few months of the year, and although it looked like Rhea Ripley might turn things around on SmackDown after WrestleMania 42, an injury has kept her out of action since May.

WWE then wisely capitalized on Chelsea Green's popularity and gave her a run with the title but never fully booked her as the face of the division. Having the belt back on Tiffany Stratton is a return to the norm as opposed to attempting to push Tatum Paxley, Jordynne Grace, Blake Monroe or anyone from Fatal Influence.

Raw's women's division has hardly been better. Liv Morgan has dominated the Women's World Championship picture but hasn't done anything out of the ordinary with the title, nor has there been a meaningful effort to give any of the other women a shot in that spot.

AEW hasn't told a ton of stories with its women in 2026, but at least the great work from Kris Statlander, Thekla, Willow Nightingale and now Mercedes Moné has made the AEW Women's World Championship picture interesting all year long.

Tag Team Wrestling Has Reached New Heights in AEW

Tag team wrestling is alive and well in AEW.

AEW prioritized tag teams out of the gate in 2019 but got away from featuring the division in a compelling way in recent years. In 2026, the division is deeper than it's ever been, including the vast amount of trios teams they have at their disposal.

Cage and Cage set the standard for the year with a superb string of matches, culminating in their terrific three-way TLC war at All Out. Along with The Young Bucks and FTR, the tag title mix has since been bolstered by the additions of The New Level, The Motor City Machine Guns, The Rascalz, The Kasper Brothers and more.

WWE, on the other hand, threw in the towel on tag team wrestling this year. They've cycled the same three or four teams in and out of the WWE Tag Team Championship picture on SmackDown with a majority of the matches blending together, while the World Tag Team Championship went four months without being defended on Raw until recently.

WWE doesn't see tag teams as a draw and that's understandable to an extent, but there have been glimmers of greatness when they have taken it seriously here and there over the years. It's been refreshing to see tag teams become a focal point again in AEW, and as a result, they've played a pivotal role in enhancing the overall product.

From a business standpoint, WWE has cooled off considerably compared to where they were in the wake of WrestleMania 40 and during John Cena's retirement tour, but attendance numbers and viewership have held steady throughout the year.

In other words, there isn't enough of an incentive for the company to change creatively. There have been brief periods where Raw and SmackDown seem to be firing on all cylinders, but maintaining that momentum has been a constant struggle.

AEW has seen their own uptick in attendance and viewership in 2026, indicating that the product they've presented has panned out and has captured the attention of their audience. There has definitely been a different vibe about AEW this year which has brought about higher fan satisfaction.

AEW has been at its worst in the past when they've worried too much about competing with WWE instead of being the best alternative they can be. Their shows could be more well rounded and certain criticisms aren't unfounded, but they've finally figured out what they've wanted to be and have established an actual identity for themselves without letting the wrestlers' creative freedom go unchecked.

That isn't to say WWE is "cooked" creatively by any means. It's been a rebuilding year for them, and once they take more risks toward the top of the card as opposed to playing it safe so frequently, they should start to see more fans gravitating back toward their shows.

AEW having such a critically-acclaimed 2026 should motivate WWE to put forth their best product possible next year and get back to what worked so well for them in the first few years of the Triple H regime.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: 5 Landing Spots for William Nylander Amid NHL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: The first quarter of the 2026-27 season has been a complete mess for the Toronto Maple Leafs.
articles.body:
The first quarter of the 2026-27 season has been a complete mess for the Toronto Maple Leafs.

After blowing a third period lead to the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday, they have lost nine games in a row, have the second-worst points percentage in the Eastern Conference and the fourth-worst points percentage in the entire NHL.

First-year head coach Jim Hiller seems to be the wrong choice, John Tavares is showing signs of age, the defense has been a mess, Sergei Bobrovsky has been one of the least productive free agent signings of the offseason and William Nylander is off to one of the worst starts of his career.

It is all enough to start wondering when significant changes might get made to the roster and organization. One of the potential changes that could be made is a trade, and given how many times Nylander has heard his name in trade speculation over the years it might start picking back up again.

Not only does Nylander have no-trade protections in his contract, he is owed $11.5 million against the cap for another five seasons and is already in his age 30 season. It is possible he has already played in his best hockey in the NHL, and might start declining sooner rather than later.

But it is also possible that he still has a lot of good years left, and that he could make a big impact for a contender.

So let's take a look at five potential landing spots if the Maple Leafs put him on the market and started listening to trade offers.

If Nylander were going to waive his no-trade protections, you would have to imagine a Stanley Cup contender would be the type of destination that would make him want to do it. The Hurricanes are not only a Stanley Cup contender, they are the defending Stanley Cup champions and look to be ready to take another serious run at it. They are the best team in the league entering play on Sunday, and while they might have a bigger need in net, they could probably fill that and still have the ability (and desire) to swing for a blockbuster elsewhere.

The Hurricanes front office is not afraid to be bold, and they are well-positioned to make some sort of a big splash before the trade deadline.

They have more than $7 million in salary cap space, a deep farm system, a talented, young defenseman in Alexander Nikishin and four first-round picks over the next three years.

And while they do not necessarily need a player like Nylander to put them over the top, it certainly wouldn't hurt their chances at repeating.

The Wild have one of the best teams in the league so far and should be in a Cup-or-Bust sort of mindset. For as good as their record is, they are extremely top-heavy with their offense and do not have a ton of scoring depth at forward beyond the top handful of players.

They do not have the salary cap space at the moment to take on Nylander's contract, and center might be a bigger need (Dylan Larkin, perhaps?) but there's another layer to this that could open them up for a major blockbuster move -- what if they trade Quinn Hughes?

Hughes is in the final year of his contract, seems to have one foot out the door, and general manager Bill Guerin will not commit one way or the other to keeping him for a potential Stanley Cup run, or trading him as to not risk losing him for nothing after the season.

If they opted to move Hughes for a return, they would almost certainly be in the market for an accompanying blockbuster move.

Perhaps a player like Nylander could, at that point, enter their radar to add some big-time scoring depth and another star-level player at forward.

Seattle probably isn't a William Nylander away from being a contender, but the Kraken have been in the market for a top-line player and star-level player for years. They need one, and they are desperate to get one, especially after some of their early first-round picks (specifically Matty Beniers and Shane Wright) have not turned into star-level players. And Wright is already playing elsewhere having been traded to the Nashville Predators.

They keep trying to add one, and they keep getting turned down.

Artemi Panarin turned them down. Jason Robertson turned them down. There have probably been others. They are not going to stop trying. It would not be a surprise if they tried to make a play for Nylander.

The only question that comes with that: Would he turn them down as well?

Seattle might actually be able to put together a package that would intrigue Toronto given the quality of the farm system, but it would all come down to Nylander's willingness to go to Seattle.

Utah is right on the edge between legitimate contender and potential pretender. There is a great young core of talent in place, and management has been extremely aggressive in adding to it since the franchise relocated. The team has a good process in place, it is playing extremely well (second-best expected goal share in the NHL), but it is still struggling to consistently win games (17th in the NHL in points percentage).

It might be missing just one thing to help bring it all together and really put the Mammoth into the NHL's upper-tier of contenders.

Another top-six winger could be it, and Utah has the prospect pool (and draft capital) to pull off a major blockbuster.

Even if it is not Nylander specifically, do not rule them out when it comes to a big in-season move.

Nikita Kucherov has made it known he is not re-signing with the Lightning, and has requested a trade out of Tampa Bay.

While the Lightning have remained adamant they are not going to move him, there is going to come a point where they have to decide if they are going to call Kucherov's bluff or not.

How's this for a hypothetical: The Lightning decide to fulfill Kucherov's request, move him before the deadline, and then take the assets they receive for him to turn around and flip them for a player like Nylander?

Nylander would probably be willing to play for a contender (and Tampa Bay absolutely still is a contender), and the Lightning would suddenly have the cap space and assets to go for something like that.

But would Toronto trade Nylander to a division rival? If the price is right, they should be open to it.

articles.title: Jessie Bates, Jordan Davis set to make Jaguars' debuts vs. Giants
articles.summary: Safety Jessie Bates and defensive tackle Jordan Davis are set to make their Jaguars debuts against the Giants.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars' defense will look a bit different on Sunday against the New York Giants .

Safety Jessie Bates and defensive tackle Jordan Davis are set to make their Jaguars debuts.

The two were acquired prior to the trade deadline, but since neither Bates nor Davis had a bye with their previous teams, the Jaguars gave them an unofficial bye last week, choosing to sit the two players against Tennessee.

Bates brings another ballhawking presence to the back-end of the Jacksonville secondary and can help cut down on some of the explosive pass plays that have hit the Jaguars' defense this season.

Davis, meanwhile, will provide a run-stuffing presence inside, but the Jaguars view him as a player who can affect the quarterback as well.

Before acquiring Bates and Davis, the Jaguars already had one of the stingiest defenses in football, ranking second in points per game allowed. Jacksonville's run defense and ability to take the ball away are two areas where this unit excels.

To land Bates, the Jaguars traded a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to Atlanta. For Davis, Jacksonville traded a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to Philadelphia.

articles.title: SEC Football Power Rankings Week 13
articles.summary: Kentucky falls in the SEC Power Rankings after three consecutive losses, while other teams move up and down.
articles.body:
Another week of college football is officially in the books, and there were several major upsets across the country over the weekend. Nebraska picked up a 31-28 victory over No. 14 Ohio State, while Washington defeated No. 8 Indiana, 27-24, in overtime. Michigan also pulled off an upset against No. 4 UCLA, earning an 18-16 victory. San Diego State added to the list by defeating No. 17 Boise State, 22-20.

The SEC also had its fair share of results worth discussing, as Missouri defeated No. 16 Kentucky, 28-14, at home. With the loss, the Wildcats have officially been eliminated from College Football Playoff contention during the first season under head coach Will Stein.

Kentucky entered its bye week with a 7-1 record but has now dropped three consecutive games. Meanwhile, several other SEC programs continue to build momentum as the regular season approaches its conclusion.

With all of that in mind, let's get into the rankings.

Georgia continues to handle business, as the Bulldogs earned a convincing 34-6 victory over South Carolina on the road.

The game remained competitive heading into halftime, with Georgia holding a 10-6 advantage. However, the Bulldogs took control in the second half, outscoring the Gamecocks 24-0 to secure another impressive victory.

It was another strong performance for head coach Kirby Smart and quarterback Gunner Stockton, as Georgia continues to look like one of the best teams in the SEC and the country.

Despite suffering its only loss of the season against Auburn on the road, Georgia remains firmly in the No. 1 spot. The Bulldogs will now look to finish the regular season on a strong note when they take on rival Georgia Tech.

Texas continues to find ways to win games, and the Longhorns put together one of their most dominant performances of the season against Arkansas.

Texas defeated the Razorbacks, 45-3, on Saturday, taking care of business against one of the SEC's struggling programs.

While the Longhorns have not always been impressive throughout the season, they have put together an impressive resume with victories over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, Missouri, and LSU.

One of the biggest reasons Texas remains at No. 2 is its head-to-head victory over Tennessee. Without that result, the Volunteers would have a strong argument for moving ahead of the Longhorns.

For now, Texas remains one of the top teams in the conference and will look to finish the regular season with another victory.

Tennessee continues to handle business, as the Volunteers defeated LSU, 27-13, at home.

Both defenses played well throughout the matchup, but Tennessee ultimately had enough on both sides of the football to pull away and secure the victory.

The Volunteers have put together an impressive season, and their victory over Alabama is one of the biggest reasons they remain inside the top three of these rankings.

However, Tennessee's head-to-head loss against Texas keeps the Volunteers behind the Longhorns. If that result had gone differently, Tennessee would have a legitimate argument for the No. 2 spot.

With another victory under their belt, the Volunteers have put themselves in a strong position heading into the College Football Playoff conversation.

Tennessee will finish the regular season against a struggling Vanderbilt team, giving the Volunteers an opportunity to close out the year with another win.

Alabama took care of business against Chattanooga on Saturday, earning a dominant 47-0 victory.

Perhaps the most impressive part of the performance was that starting quarterback Keelon Russell did not play as he continues to recover from an ankle injury. Despite his absence, the Crimson Tide had no trouble handling their opponent.

Alabama remains at No. 4 because of its two losses against Georgia and Tennessee. While the Crimson Tide have been impressive throughout the season and have blown out several opponents, those head-to-head defeats keep them behind the Bulldogs and Volunteers.

If Russell can return to full health, Alabama will remain a dangerous team heading into the postseason.

The Crimson Tide will now turn their attention to their biggest rivalry matchup of the season, as they prepare to face Auburn to close out the regular season.

Oklahoma makes one of the biggest jumps in this week's rankings, moving all the way into the top five.

The Sooners defeated Ole Miss last week before following that performance with another impressive victory against Texas A&M, winning 28-7 on Saturday.

Oklahoma has now put together some momentum following the firing of former offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle and the decision to promote tight ends coach Jason Witten to the offensive coordinator position.

The Sooners have also picked up some impressive victories throughout the season, including their head-to-head win over Texas.

With several teams ranked ahead of them suffering losses and Oklahoma continuing to win games, the Sooners have earned their spot at No. 5.

Now, Oklahoma will have another opportunity to build its resume when it travels to face Missouri next week. That matchup will be important for both programs as they look to finish the regular season on a positive note.

Florida comes in at No. 6 after picking up back-to-back victories against Kentucky on the road and Vanderbilt at home.

The Gators have put together some impressive wins this season, including victories over Ole Miss at home and Texas and Kentucky on the road.

Florida got off to a strong start, opening the season with a 4-0 record. However, the Gators hit a rough stretch, going 1-4 over their next five games before bouncing back with two consecutive victories.

Their win over Kentucky was particularly impressive, as Florida traveled to Lexington and defeated the Wildcats during an important stretch of the season.

Now, the Gators have an opportunity to finish the regular season on a three-game winning streak. They will look to carry their recent momentum into their final matchup against rival Florida State.

Missouri moves up to No. 7 after taking care of business against Kentucky, earning a 28-14 victory at home.

The Tigers entered the matchup as favorites and were able to deliver a strong performance against the Wildcats, handing Kentucky its third consecutive loss.

Missouri has not necessarily put together an impressive resume this season, with its biggest victory arguably coming against Florida at home in a 45-17 win. However, defeating Kentucky was another important result for the Tigers.

Missouri has shown flashes of being a competitive team throughout the year, but consistency has been an issue.

Now, the Tigers will have another opportunity to pick up an important victory when they host Oklahoma on Saturday. It will be an interesting matchup, especially with both teams coming off impressive wins.

Kentucky slides all the way to No. 8 after suffering a 28-14 loss to Missouri on the road.

For the Wildcats, it has been an impressive first season under head coach Will Stein, especially considering the expectations entering the year. However, the way the season has unfolded over the past few weeks has been disappointing.

Kentucky entered its bye week with a 7-1 record, with its only loss coming against Alabama. Since then, the Wildcats have lost three consecutive games against Tennessee, Florida, and Missouri.

The latest defeat officially eliminates Kentucky from College Football Playoff contention, putting an end to what had been an exciting season for the program.

While the losing streak is disappointing, Kentucky has still accomplished plenty during Stein's first season. Not many people expected the Wildcats to reach seven wins, and they have already secured a winning record in SEC play.

Now, Kentucky has one final opportunity to finish the regular season on a positive note when it hosts Louisville. A victory would give the Wildcats an 8-4 record and provide some momentum heading into the offseason.

Ole Miss falls one spot to No. 9 despite earning a convincing 59-17 victory over Wofford at home.

The Rebels took care of business against an opponent they were expected to defeat, but several teams previously ranked below them picked up important victories over the weekend.

Ole Miss has put together some impressive wins this season, including victories over Louisville, LSU, and Missouri. However, the Rebels have also struggled to find consistency throughout the year under first-year head coach Pete Golding.

With the regular season approaching its conclusion, Ole Miss has one more important rivalry matchup remaining.

The Rebels will take on Mississippi State in the Egg Bowl, giving them an opportunity to finish the regular season with another victory and potentially move back into the top half of the SEC rankings.

Auburn took care of business against Samford on Saturday, earning a convincing 59-17 victory at home.

The Tigers have been one of the more inconsistent teams in the SEC this season, but they have managed to become bowl-eligible under first-year head coach Alex Golesh.

While Auburn has struggled against some of the conference's better teams, the Tigers have also picked up one of the biggest victories of the season by defeating Georgia at home.

That victory continues to be one of the biggest reasons Auburn remains inside the top 10 of these rankings.

Now, the Tigers will have one final opportunity to make a statement before the postseason when they travel to face rival Alabama.

It will certainly be a difficult matchup, but Auburn would love nothing more than to finish the regular season by upsetting the Crimson Tide.

LSU falls to No. 11 after struggling offensively against Tennessee, suffering a 27-13 loss on the road.

The Tigers were unable to generate enough offense to keep up with the Volunteers, resulting in another disappointing defeat during what has been a frustrating season.

Entering the year, many LSU fans had much higher expectations under head coach Lane Kiffin and quarterback Sam Leavitt. However, things have not gone according to plan.

LSU has managed to pick up only six victories, with its wins coming against Texas A&M, Mississippi State, and Auburn in SEC play.

While the Tigers have had some opportunities to turn things around, they have struggled to put together consistent performances against the conference's better teams.

Now, LSU will have one final opportunity to finish SEC play on a positive note when it travels to face Arkansas.

A victory would improve the Tigers to 7-5 overall and 4-5 in conference play, giving them something positive to build on heading into the offseason.

No. 12 South Carolina Gamecocks (6-5, 4-5)

South Carolina falls to No. 12 after suffering a disappointing 34-6 loss against Georgia at home.

The Gamecocks actually managed to keep things competitive in the first half, trailing the Bulldogs by only four points at halftime. However, Georgia completely took control after the break, outscoring South Carolina 24-0 in the second half.

South Carolina has experienced plenty of ups and downs throughout the season. The Gamecocks started the year 2-0 before losing three consecutive games. They then managed to turn things around with four straight victories, but have now dropped their last two matchups.

It has been a frustrating stretch for head coach Shane Beamer and the Gamecocks, especially after showing signs of improvement earlier in the year.

Unfortunately, the schedule does not get any easier, as South Carolina will close out the regular season against rival Clemson.

The Gamecocks will have to regroup quickly if they hope to finish the season with another victory.

No. 13 Mississippi State Bulldogs (5-6, 1-6)

Mississippi State improved to 5-6 on the season after defeating Tennessee Tech, 34-16, at home.

The Bulldogs have struggled throughout the year, especially after losing star quarterback Kamario Taylor to a season-ending injury.

His absence has played a major role in Mississippi State's struggles, as the Bulldogs have had difficulty finding consistency offensively.

However, Mississippi State still has an opportunity to accomplish an important goal before the regular season comes to an end.

The Bulldogs will travel to face rival Ole Miss in the Egg Bowl, with bowl eligibility on the line. It certainly will not be an easy matchup, but a victory would give Mississippi State its sixth win of the season.

It would also be a huge accomplishment for the Bulldogs after everything they have experienced throughout the year.

Arkansas drops to No. 14 after suffering a disappointing 45-3 loss against Texas on the road.

The Razorbacks were unable to compete with the Longhorns, as Texas controlled the matchup from start to finish.

While Arkansas has not put together the best season, the Razorbacks have managed to pick up a couple of victories in SEC play, including wins over Vanderbilt and South Carolina.

There have been plenty of growing pains during the first season under head coach Ryan Silverfield, but the program has an opportunity to learn from this season and make improvements moving forward.

For now, Arkansas will look to finish the regular season on a positive note when it hosts LSU.

A victory would give the Razorbacks another SEC win and provide some momentum heading into the offseason.

Vanderbilt continues to struggle throughout the season after losing star quarterback Diego Pavia following his graduation.

The Commodores decided to turn to five-star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis, who has experienced some growing pains while adjusting to college football.

However, there have been signs of improvement from Curtis, and Vanderbilt will hope he continues to develop as the season progresses.

The Commodores most recently suffered a 35-27 loss against Florida on the road. While Vanderbilt managed to keep the game competitive, the Gators ultimately did enough to secure the victory.

Unfortunately, the schedule does not get any easier, as Vanderbilt will close out the regular season against Tennessee.

The Volunteers have been one of the better teams in the SEC this season, making this another difficult challenge for the Commodores.

Texas A&M remains at No. 16, as the Aggies continue to be one of the most disappointing teams in the SEC this season.

After reaching the College Football Playoff last year, expectations were much higher entering the 2026 campaign. Unfortunately, things have not gone according to plan.

The Aggies traveled to Norman on Saturday to face Oklahoma but struggled to generate offense, suffering a 28-7 loss.

Texas A&M has now lost five consecutive SEC games, with its last conference victory coming against Arkansas on Oct. 3.

It has been a difficult stretch for the Aggies, who have struggled to find consistency on both sides of the football.

Now, Texas A&M will have one final opportunity to end the regular season on a positive note when it hosts rival Texas.

It will be a difficult matchup, but the Aggies will hope to pull off an upset and finish the season with a 5-7 record and a 2-7 mark in SEC play.

articles.title: “Extremely Disrespectful,” “That Is Mean Hearted”: Fans Slam Tennessee Banner Dragging Dolly Parton Into Lane Kiffin Rivalry
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin’s return to Knoxville on Saturday wasn’t received well by Tennessee fans. During the game, a plane flew over the stadium with a banner reading “D...
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin's return to Knoxville on Saturday wasn't received well by Tennessee fans. During the game, a plane flew over the stadium with a banner reading "Dolly hated Kiffin," referencing the late country music icon.

Tennessee fans have often given Kiffin a hostile reception because he left the team for USC in 2009. However, the decision to bring Dolly Parton into the equation did not sit well with several fans on social media. They questioned the banner's message and argued that the legendary singer should not be associated with the hostility surrounding Kiffin.

"Extremely disrespectful to Dolly's name," one fan commented.

"Dolly did not hate anyone. That is mean hearted. She was a great woman," another fan wrote.

Another fan wrote, "Tennessee still hating Kiffin is the softest thing in sports."

"Dolly didnt hate anybody but she might likely call Lane a no count and add a Bless His Heart for good measure …she had a kind way of speaking truth ❤️," the fan commented.

"I'm almost positive Dolly didn't have a hateful bone in her body," another added.

According to USA Today, the Volunteers are paying tribute to Parton this season with a commemorative helmet sticker featuring the word "Dolly" above a butterfly, an insect widely associated with the late singer.

Lane Kiffin Reacts to Tennessee Fans Throwing Golf Balls

The banner was not the only controversial incident during Kiffin's return to Knoxville. Tennessee fans also threw golf balls and mustard bottles onto the field, causing the game to stop with more than three minutes remaining.

Kiffin joked afterward that fans had listened to Josh Heupel's comments at SEC Media Days about buying golf balls, while making it clear he wasn't criticizing the Tennessee coach.

"I'm laughing at it. They listened to their coach. No, that doesn't surprise me," he said in a press conference.

Kiffin even spoke highly of Tennessee fans, giving them credit for today's win.

"I didn't think it was very toxic early on in warmups, coming into the stadium. I had some coaches that had been with us say, 'Oh, this is going to be nothing like Ole Miss. They're going to actually be, like, kind of nice.' They were like, 'Oh, they're not going to be nice when we go back out there. Like I said, I don't know that I've ever credited a crowd before. They did a great job changing the game today. Truly like having a 12th man on defense," Kiffin said.

articles.title: Jim Hiller Insists He Hasn't Lost Maple Leafs' Room After 'Fire Hiller' Chants Punctuate 9th Straight Loss
articles.summary: With the Maple Leafs' winless skid reaching nine games after a late 4-3 collapse against the Blue Jackets, a distraught Jim Hiller acknowledged fan frustrati...
articles.body:
Jim Hiller, who appeared distraught and out of answers, insists he has not lost the Toronto Maple Leafs' room after the club's winless streak reached nine games with a 4-3 loss to the Columbus Blue Jackets at Scotiabank Arena.

Chants of "Fire Hiller" filled the building in the final minutes as the Leafs surrendered a third-period lead, sharpening the edge of a night that already felt like another low point. Hiller was asked directly if he believed he had lost the room.

"No, I don't believe that," he said. "Just because of my interactions with them and what I hear. That's how I feel."

He did not pretend the noise was irrelevant. When asked about the fan unrest, he answered without deflection.

"I'd be pissed too. I mean, we all would be, wouldn't we?"

On the chants themselves and the job security that now sits in plain view, Hiller was blunt.

"Well, I mean, the noise is the noise. It's always going to be there. I understand that. I don't know. I've got to do some soul searching here. There's no question. And we've got to get the team better prepared than we did tonight. That's the bottom line. Players play, we've got to coach them, and we've got to do a better job because that's not good enough."

The collapse marked the first time this season the Leafs lost in regulation after leading through two periods. They entered the third period ahead 3-2 and watched the Blue Jackets score twice in less than a minute late in the period, the second coming from Zach Werenski with 3:28 remaining. The sequence drew the loudest "Fire Hiller" chants of the night.

The nine-game winless stretch has already forced Hiller to move away from an early-season approach that was widely viewed as stubborn . He had largely stuck with similar forward combinations and defensive pairings through the first half of the skid, giving certain groups extended rope. After the seventh consecutive loss, he began to change things up , elevating Gavin McKenna, dropping William Nylander at times and shuffling the middle of the lineup in search of chemistry that has not arrived.

The organization has also tried external resets. On Nov. 13, the Leafs spent a day at the ballpark, taking batting practice at Rogers Centre in an attempt to step away from the rink and the results. The day before Saturday's game against Columbus, they turned a scheduled practice into an optional skate after spending roughly two hours with golf star Rory McIlroy and sports psychologist Bob Rotella . Hiller described the message as one about bringing joy back to the game. It did not produce a win the following night.

Hiller was asked why the same mistakes, or variations of them, keep appearing and whether belief is still intact.

"Well, I mean, I always keep the belief. That's what we have to do. I mean, you've got to believe that you're going to write the best story after this game tonight, right? And then the next one, you've got to believe you're going to write even a better one. And so that's just what we do. And if you don't have that belief, you don't make it to this level. So that's just what people do. But our resolve, our resolve, I think, is the bigger issue, not the belief. It's the resolve because it gets hard, and it is hard right now. So how do you answer that? How do you answer? And we haven't answered that very well."

When pressed on what else the coaching staff can do after already trying different combinations and approaches, he offered little beyond persistence.

"Yeah. Well, keep trying. Get on to page 10 or 11 or whatever of the playbook or of the options, of the approaches. You got to keep trying."

The possible return of Kirill Marchenko was raised. Hiller said it would help, but made clear there are no saviors on the way.

"That will help us. But there's no saviors coming. We could get three or four more guys if we do some of the things we did. You're going to get the same result. So, yeah, that would be great to get them. They'll help us whenever they arrive. But can't do that and expect to win."

He returned to the final three minutes and the plays that cost the Leafs the game.

"We've had stretches, and it gets you excited because you think you can see what you can do. And then for whatever reasons, we have moments like we had tonight, which is, it's just not, it's not National Hockey League level. And that's frustrating for all of us. And when I say all of us, I mean everybody. I mean everybody. Players, media, fans, anybody. Anybody. It's hard to swallow."

The Maple Leafs fell to 8-14-3 on the season. Remarkably, their goal differential sits at just -12, a reflection of how close many of the games in this nine-game skid have been. That doesn't make it any easier for fans who don't see a path to success under the current leadership.

Eight of the nine games have been at Scotiabank Arena. The Leafs will practice at home on Sunday before embarking on a three-game road trip that begins on Long Island, with stops to follow in Boston and Pittsburgh. Perhaps getting away from the "noise" will help.

But the status quo isn't working, even if, for now, the Leafs don't appear to have any appetite for a coaching change.

articles.title: Official | PSG confirm Désiré Doué ACL injury
