articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain have confirmed that Désiré Doué (21) has sustained an ACL injury in his right knee.

Doué went down without contact during Saturday night's win over OGC Nice at the Allianz Riviera. Just moments earlier, the France international had given his side the lead against OGC Nice, and immediately clutched his right knee. The stretcher was called for seconds later, and the France international left the field in tears, with eight minutes added on to the end of the first half.

In a post-match press conference attended by Get French Football News, Luis Enrique provided an update on the Frenchman's health: "We will have to wait until tomorrow to know, but it is a serious injury . He is sad and worried. He will come back stronger than ever."

On Sunday afternoon, PSG confirmed that Doué had torn his ACL in his right knee. The club also confirmed that the forward would undergo surgery before the end of the month. Both he and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who suffered the same injury last month, will miss the vast majority if not the remainder of the season.

articles.title: Argentina's Leandro collapses mid-interview after Boca Juniors' Copa Sudamericana win
articles.summary: BARRANQUILLA, Colombia (AP) — Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes fainted during a post-match interview after the Copa Sudamericana final.Paredes collapsed...
articles.body:
BARRANQUILLA, Colombia (AP) — Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes fainted during a post-match interview after the Copa Sudamericana final.

Paredes collapsed a few moments after he started answering a reporter's question following Boca Juniors' 2-0 win over Atletico Mineiro on Saturday in Barranquilla, Colombia.

"Now it's time to enjoy it with my teammates, be thankful for what we've experienced..." Paredes said when his gaze went blank before he could finish the sentence.

He fell back as the interviewer from broadcaster DSports tried unsuccessfully to break his fall.

Paredes was treated on the field briefly before getting back to his feet. He then waved to the applauding crowd as he jogged toward the locker rooms.

He later posted on Instagram that he was OK, alongside a photo of himself smiling.

Paredes had been substituted in the 58th minute.

articles.title: Ottawa Charge Enter New Season With Clear Intent And Vision For Success
articles.summary: The Charge enter the season with high expectations following another trip to the Walter Cup Finals, but understand that a stronger start to the season and es...
articles.body:
Three days and two on-ice sessions later, training camp for the Ottawa Charge is well underway. A theme throughout these first few days has been intensity, as each player has shown up with clear intent, and management has set clear expectations.

"Focus is an important piece for us," said head coach Carla MacLeod. "Belief and determined. We've been to the Walter Cup Final two years in a row, which in and of itself is a strong accomplishment. But in our industry, you want to win the Walter Cup. We're always at our best when we're enjoying what we're doing, but it's not without an attention to detail."

Several themes have already emerged in the first few days of Charge training camp that should excite fans, and intensity is at the top of that list. Across two on-ice sessions at the Bell Sensplex in Ottawa's west end, it's been the name of the game: this group is expected to give everything on every shift and drive home the message that no one wants to play against them.

Players are taking each drill as seriously as a playoff game, bringing speed, tenacity, and grit. Those have become important attributes for Ottawa Charge hockey over the years, so seeing them early in camp is a positive.

Another theme is the focus on starting the season with a winning record, something that has eluded the organization, with losing records in each of the prior three seasons' opening months. These slow, inconsistent starts have added pressure as the season winds down, putting the group in a position where late-season winning streaks have become a necessity. While the team has made back-to-back Walter Cup Finals, the coaching staff has already made it clear, both in meetings and on the ice, that starting the season above .500 is essential and non-negotiable. And the message has clearly been heard.

The Ottawa Charge speak following start of training camp

Following three seasons under the leadership of Brianne Jenner, the Ottawa Charge find themselves in search of their next captain, rather large skates to fill. Several options stand out, led by Rebecca Leslie, a long-time teammate of Jenner and someone Leslie has looked up to, especially since arriving in the nation's capital.

"Obviously, losing Brianne (Jenner) and Emily (Clark), they were people in our locker room that were very important," said Leslie. "Personally, I've learned a lot from Brianne. She's someone I've looked up to for a long time. She's someone who leads by example and works hard every day, and so was Emily. So we try to bring those qualities into the locker room."

While options remain and no decisions have been made yet, management points out the importance of having five of the team's seven members from last year's group back this season.

"There are different types of leaders, we all know that," said general manager Mike Hirshfeld. "We're obviously looking for people who can motivate others, can be a helping hand, can push other players. There are a lot of factors involved, but we feel like we have a good group in that locker room. We'll make a decision very shortly on that."

Every team experienced roster changes this offseason through expansion, the draft, and free agency, some more so than others, and the Charge are no different. The loss of Jenner and Emily Clark, in particular, original members of the franchise, among others, has left holes in the lineup. Those holes create opportunities for camp invites and talented draft selections, and there are plenty to choose from.

"We're really excited about building into this season and who we have on our roster," said MacLeod. "It'll be a competitive training camp. We're grateful for everyone who has got us to this point, but now you look forward and make sure that we're aligned with our goals and getting better. We're excited about what we can accomplish this year."

An encouraging sign for Charge fans is that this group has brought an intensity to camp unmatched in past training camps, so narrowing the list to only a few names feels like an injustice. That said, it's important to highlight the players who have stood out most throughout camp.

Annalise Wong, a camp invite out of the University of British Columbia, has certainly been a standout. She may be listed as 5'2", but she plays as though she's a foot taller. She's the first in front of the net, first to join the rush and has the edge work to be a difference-maker on the team.

Jenna Buglioni, acquired this offseason from the Seattle Torrent, has been noticeable beyond the expected grit and strength along the boards. Her speed and faceoff skills have been standout attributes so far.

Draft picks Vivian Jungels and Jordan Ray have also been impressive, skating with ease, making smart passes and being in the right place at the right time.

Ronja Savolainen, who had offseason surgery, has been rehabbing throughout the summer and has been a full participant through training camp thus far.

The group has two more practices in Ottawa before heading to Hamilton to face the Detroit Clutch on November 23 and the Toronto Sceptres on November 24.

articles.title: Sheffield United 4-0 Watford: Blades Sting Hornets at Bramall Lane
articles.summary: Sheffield United completely dismantled Watford in a 4-0 win at Bramall Lane on Saturday afternoon.Ben Brereton Diaz scored a quick brace inside the first few...
articles.body:
Sheffield United completely dismantled Watford in a 4-0 win at Bramall Lane on Saturday afternoon.

Ben Brereton Diaz scored a quick brace inside the first few minutes to get the Blades off to a flyer; a 20-yard strike was followed up by a coolly dispatched penalty.

Jordan Ayew made it three in the second half when he met Tahith Chong's corner with a header. With just a few minutes to spare, Sydie Peck found himself on the scoresheet once more with a neat left-footed finish in front of the Kop.

Blades: Cooper, Arblaster (Riedewald 74), Tanganga, Choudhury, Ayew (Bamford 74), Donovan (Cannon 65), Burrows, Kitching, Chong (McCallum 82), Brereton Díaz (Campbell 82), Peck.

Unused: Davies, Shackleton, McGuinness, Baptiste.

Watford: Ravaglia, Coulibaly (Mlacic 59), Keben, Pollock, Bola, Bravo (Bove 69), Doumbia (Kjerrumgaard 79)h, Payero (Kyprianou 69), Traoré Kayembe, Mavididi (Nabizada 59).

Unused: Bachmann, Vata, Zemura, Grieves.

A long ball forward early on from Kitching caused problems for the Watford defence, with Coulibaly challenging Donovan in the air before the ball fell kindly for Brereton Diaz. The Chilean made no mistake, keeping his composure to fire a low finish into the bottom corner and give the hosts an early advantage.

Things went from bad to worse for the visitors shortly afterwards. Peck was brought down by Payero as he attempted to create room for a shot inside the penalty area, leaving referee Robinson with little hesitation before pointing to the spot. Brereton Diaz stepped up and confidently dispatched the resulting penalty, sending Ravaglia the wrong way to double United's lead.

The Blades continued to threaten as the first half progressed, although Donovan was left frustrated after receiving a booking for simulation when attempting to win a decision while driving forward. The Brentford loanee subsequently tested Ravaglia with an effort on goal, but the Watford goalkeeper was equal to it.

Chong thought he had added a third in the second half, only for his effort to be ruled out for offside. Ayew also came close when he met Donovan's delivery, but Ravaglia reacted well to keep out his attempt at the near post.

Watford briefly believed they had found a route back into the contest after the interval, with substitute Bove finding the net, only for the assistant referee's flag to rule out the effort for offside.

United, meanwhile, continued to look the more dangerous side and eventually extended their advantage on 61 minutes. Peck threaded an excellent pass into Chong, who showed good strength and footwork to get beyond Bola before delivering into the danger area. Ayew was perfectly positioned to meet the opportunity, guiding a close-range header beyond Ravaglia to make it three.

With the game firmly under control, Wilder introduced Riedewald and Bamford as the Blades looked to see out the remaining stages while maintaining their attacking threat.

There was still time for United to put the finishing touches on an impressive afternoon, with the fourth goal arriving in the 84th minute. Bamford played an important role in the build-up, setting up Peck inside the penalty area before the midfielder calmly side-footed a left-footed effort into the far corner.

articles.title: What Luka Doncic said to LA Lakers coaches as frustration with teammates becomes evident
articles.summary: Luka Doncic has helped the LA Lakers get off to a stellar start this season, but their form in the last few games has raised some concern. The Lakers’ loss t...
articles.body:
Luka Doncic has helped the LA Lakers get off to a stellar start this season, but their form in the last few games has raised some concern.

The Lakers' loss to the Charlotte Hornets might appear to some as a one-off in a run of stellar wins, but fans who have watched them in recent weeks have seen that there are some serious problems.

In particular, the Lakers' defensive woes have been on full display, especially while they play against much weaker teams.

Luka Doncic blasts LA Lakers stars for getting 'blown by' opponents

A clip of Luka Doncic complaining to the LA Lakers coaches has recently gone viral, in which he is seen sharing his frustration with his teammates.

In particular, he is seemingly referencing Jake LaRavia, Sandro Mamukelashvili, and Jarred Vanderbilt not putting up enough of a fight against their rivals on the defensive end.

"Show every f****** clip of everybody getting blown by! Every f****** time!"

Some fans might empathise with Doncic, as he felt that his stellar work on the offensive end was being undone by the lacklustre defensive effort from his teammates.

However, there is a fair argument to be made against Doncic, who is known for being one of the weakest defenders among superstars in the NBA.

If Doncic wants to hold his teammates accountable for their defensive effort, he needs to begin delivering at a higher level on the defensive end himself.

And while he has shown an improved level of commitment on the defensive end compared to years past this season, Doncic is still by no means a stellar or even average defender.

One has to imagine that his teammates will feel a level of frustration over Doncic's comments going public, as it puts an enhanced spotlight on them, thus causing their every move to be scrutinised even further.

articles.title: Texas A&M women's tennis unveils 2026 national championship rings
articles.summary: Texas A&M women's tennis received its 2026 national championship rings after defeating Auburn to capture its second NCAA title in three seasons.
articles.body:
Texas A&M women's tennis added another lasting reminder of its historic 2026 season as the Aggies received their national championship rings earlier this month.

The team received its rings on Nov. 2, celebrating a championship run that brought Texas A&M its second national title in three seasons. The moment served as another opportunity to recognize a program that has established itself among the best in college tennis.

The Aggies captured their latest championship in May, defeating Auburn 4-1 in the NCAA title match. Texas A&M finished the season 28-5 and reached the national championship match for the third consecutive year under head coach Mark Weaver. Daria Smetannikov earned NCAA Championship Most Outstanding Player honors following the title run. She was joined on the All-Tournament Team by Lucciana Perez, Mia Kupres, Lexington Reed and Violeta Martinez.

Perez also put together one of the most impressive individual seasons in program history. She finished as the nation's No. 1 player and became the first Aggie to complete an undefeated singles campaign, posting a perfect 28-0 record. For Weaver, the latest championship further solidified what he has built in College Station. Texas A&M has now won two national titles in three years while making three consecutive appearances in the championship match.

The championship rings provide another reminder of those accomplishments, but the program's focus has already shifted toward maintaining that standard.

With the fall portion of the 2026-27 season underway, the Aggies are preparing for another run at a national championship.

articles.summary: We're looking at five key matchups to watch when the Eagles host the Steelers in Week 11
articles.body:
The Eagles return from their bye Sunday with DeVonta Smith back in the lineup and a seven-game losing streak to end. For Smith's return to make a difference against Pittsburgh, Philadelphia has to give Joe Milton time to throw. That starts with right tackle Markel Bell against T.J. Watt.

Milton took seven sacks against the Giants in his first start for Philadelphia. If Jordan Mailata can handle Alex Highsmith on his own, the Eagles can send help to Bell and still give Smith time to get downfield. On defense, the first test without Zack Baun comes against Jaylen Warren, who has already gained more than 1,000 yards from scrimmage.

With the opening kickoff fast approaching, here are the five key matchups to watch.

Watt has 7.5 sacks and can shorten a passing play before Milton gets to his second read. Watch Dallas Goedert and Saquon Barkley when the Eagles need to throw. A chip can buy Bell time to get into position, but it also delays the release of a receiver Milton might need underneath. The snaps where Bell gets no help will tell Philadelphia how much of the playbook it can use on third down.

2. Alex Highsmith against Jordan Mailata

Highsmith has 3.5 sacks. Mailata's value will show up in what the Eagles can do elsewhere if he wins his matchup without help. On longer drops, he has to keep Highsmith from turning the corner and give Milton room to step forward. If Mailata can do that consistently, Philadelphia can put more of its protection toward Watt and still give Smith and Makai Lemon time to work downfield.

3. Cameron Heyward against the Eagles' interior line

Getting Milton to step up only helps if there's somewhere to go. Heyward can take that space away by driving a guard back toward the quarterback. Landon Dickerson, Drew Kendall and Tyler Steen will have to sort out where the interior help goes, especially if Pittsburgh moves Heyward before the snap. The same matchup matters on early downs, when Barkley needs a clean path through the middle to keep the Eagles out of third-and-long.

Metcalf leads Pittsburgh with 432 receiving yards. Quinyon Mitchell has allowed a 64.4 passer rating when targeted, sixth among qualifying cornerbacks, leaving Woolen as a tempting option to attack. Watch which side Pittsburgh sends Metcalf to on obvious passing downs and whether Philadelphia keeps a safety over top of him. If Aaron Rodgers sees single coverage, he can give Metcalf a chance to win at the catch point even when the cornerback is in position.

5. Jaylen Warren against the Eagles' linebackers

Warren enters with 719 rushing yards and 320 receiving yards. With Baun on injured reserve, Jihaad Campbell and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. are expected to start together. Pittsburgh can make them step forward to fit the run on early downs, then ask them to follow Warren into the flat on third down. A tackle short of the sticks can end the drive even when Rodgers gets the completion

articles.title: Fernandes puts contract talks on hold and focuses on reviving Man Utd
articles.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes says there are no ongoing negotiations over a new contract for him to stay at Old Trafford. The 32-year-old’s futur...
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes says there are no ongoing negotiations over a new contract for him to stay at Old Trafford.

The 32-year-old's future is still up in the air after it was revealed he turned down a second contract offer from the club, with his current deal due to expire at the end of the season.

The Portugal international's form has dropped off this season and has only managed one goal and assist since his hat-trick against Ipswich in August.

Bruno, who has amassed 341 appearances for the Red Devils, says the club offered him a new deal but he does not think it is the right time for negotiations.

He told Sky Sports: "The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay.

"There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here.

"I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

"I've always showed how much I care about this club and how much I want to win at this club. I've always said, the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on.

The Red Devils sit in the relegation zone ahead of their clash with Liverpool after winning just once from their opening 10 games, which led to Michael Carrick being sacked and replaced with Mauricio Pochettino.

Bruno says his contract talks have been put "to a side" and thinks the first priority should be to get back to winning games.

"We spoke about the contract at the end of last season," he added.

"We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

"The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games."

articles.title: Seedy K’s GameCap: Pittsburgh
articles.summary: Back in the day when I attended just about every rock & roll show, whether I knew the music of the headliners or not, I was held hostage by more than a few i...
articles.body:
Back in the day when I attended just about every rock & roll show, whether I knew the music of the headliners or not, I was held hostage by more than a few inept opening acts.

There was a group from Cincy — blessedly can't remember their name — who appeared too often. The nephew of a guy name Dino who promoted a lot of shows in the Tri-State area played bass or something like that.

A literally unlistenable ensemble named Songcatcher opened for the Neville Brothers Band. Walked out on their set in New Orleans. A few months later I ventured to the lobby at a show here as soon as they were announced.

Then on the Thanksgiving evening in the Queen City when The Dood and I heard Derek & the Dominos (No Skydog) on their one tour, the lackluster opening group was named Toe Fat.

Such musings came to mind while comparing U of L's opening thirty minute performance Saturday night against Pittsburgh with that after intermission.

U of L's Defense, as it has been for most of this six game win streak, was steady and solid.

The pittance of 150 yards surrendered, only 8 First Downs.

Yes, the Panthers' QB position was masquerading as a game of Musical Chairs, but still . . .

U of L with the ball in the opening half.

Which was statistically offset by a triad of sacks for -31.

A pick that led to Pitt's other three points.

U of L was gifted the ball four times inside the Panthers' thirty yard line.

The running game was to be honest inconsequential.

143 positive yards were offset by 56 negative.

But, my oh my, how about that Manly Man No Old Spice Necessary 15 play 10:16 4th Q clock eater for the Cards' final TD.

Complemented a dozen Kejuan Brown ram jam bam smashmouth rushes.

You could see the approving pipe smoke emanating from Schnell's gravestone chimney.

The quality of the Cardinal AFROS was also on display.

Of the 309 yards receiving, 203 were Yards After Catch.

Pitt is pretty mediocre, especially with its QB issues.

But, for the final thirty minutes, U of L whomped 'em up the side of the head as they were supposed to.

articles.title: Andy Farrell praises Sam Prendergast’s response after South Africa criticism
articles.summary: Fly-half Prendergast ultimately landed the decisive penalty in Saturday’s statement win over the world champions
articles.body:
Andy Farrell believes Sam Prendergast emerged from a pre-match storm fuelled by South Africa 's coaching staff to show exactly what he is capable of.

Fly-half Prendergast ultimately landed the decisive penalty in Saturday's statement 20-17 win over the world champions in Dublin after avoiding retrospective punishment for a hip-drop tackle against Fiji.

Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus branded Prendergast's challenge "terrible" but predicted he would be cleared to play on a "technicality" during a controversial press conference on Monday.

Erasmus' assistant Mzwandile Stick continued the criticism on Friday, saying: "If that was a Fijian player, he would be sitting in Fiji now doing some extra lessons of how to tackle."

Ireland head coach Farrell made clear his unhappiness with the inflammatory comments from the opposition camp as he praised Prendergast's response.

"I didn't like all that," he said. "It carried on during the week as well, didn't it? I didn't like all that about Sam because Sam was cleared, and I was there while he was cleared.

"Sam's done nothing wrong and I was so proud of him in the sense that he played like that.

"Nothing bothered him, I thought he was excellent. He had the courage to play the balls out the back, play quickly, and play to space. I thought it was an excellent game from him all round."

After Robert Baloucoune scored two first-half tries and Ronan Kelleher added another, Prendergast nervelessly split the posts from distance in the 54th minute before a heroic defensive display secured victory.

Prendergast, 23, also received a glowing endorsement from half-back partner Jamison Gibson-Park.

"He's come on leaps and bounds I think in the last little while," said the scrum-half.

"He's just taken it all in his stride and the most impressive thing is he's just able to bounce into the next moment and I know that's something he's working hard on but I'm pretty proud of the guy.

"He's been through a lot and he's playing some good footy so I'm very happy for him."

Ireland laid down a marker ahead of next year's World Cup with an overdue – and thoroughly deserved – success over one of rugby's top-ranked nations.

Their scrum was comprehensively outmuscled by South Africa in a 24-13 Dublin defeat last November, while they have lost their last four meetings with New Zealand and last two with France.

Farrell has now won four of six encounters with the Springboks after celebrating another memorable victory of his reign, secured in front of a capacity Aviva Stadium crowd.

"It's another massive game so it has to be up there (as one of the best)," he said.

"It's what we also expect of ourselves – not to beat South Africa but to keep growing and delivering, certainly at home. It certainly matters a lot to us."

Captain Dan Sheehan, who started at number eight for the first time at Test level, relished the challenge of taking on a different role having won his previous 42 caps at hooker.

He said: "It wasn't perfect by any means but something different keeps your mind busy and almost gives me a distraction from thinking about the game too much.

"I was pretty happy with how the lads fronted up, especially in the pack. I thought we kept our calm pretty well at times and backed ourselves when it mattered.

"We talked about it all week, about making sure we front up on big days like this and the privilege of having the world champions in our back garden and for lads to show up meant a lot."

Ireland will play Australia in the Nations Championship fifth-place final at Twickenham on Friday evening.

articles.title: England’s Will Jacks out of T20 Australia tour due to broken hand
articles.summary: Tom Banton has been promoted to vice-captain after Will Jacks was injured in the Melbourne series opener
articles.body:
Will Jacks has been ruled out of the remainder of England's white-ball tour of Australia after suffering a broken hand in the series opener.

Jacks left the field with blood streaming from his right hand after attempting a tough caught-and-bowled chance of Ben Dwarshuis, which came in the penultimate over of the first T20 in Melbourne.

It was later confirmed to be a fracture, meaning he will miss the chance to captain England for the first time, with Tom Banton to step up as vice-captain in his absence.

With regular skipper Harry Brook missing the fifth and final T20 ahead of the Test series against South Africa, Jacks had been pencilled in to the take charge in Canberra on 2 December.

Banton has been chosen as Brook's deputy ahead of more experienced candidates after impressing the coaching staff since returning to the international fold, proving himself a quietly influential voice and making the most of opportunities afforded by injuries to Jacob Bethell and Jos Buttler.

Having already turned his temporary elevation to opener in the ODI side into a strong bid to be first-choice at next year's World Cup, the Somerset man has now been formally added to the officer ranks.

Speaking at the end of the 50-over series, head coach Brendon McCullum namechecked the 28-year-old's growing status as someone who "exhibits the behaviours and understands the direction of travel you want from the team".

England are weighing up possible replacements for Jacks, having already called up Hampshire's Scott Currie to bolster numbers when Brook and Jordan Cox miss the fifth game.

As a spin bowling all-rounder with the ability to add power to the lower middle order, Rehan Ahmed would appear to be the closest to a like-for-like replacement.

The 22-year-old signed a one-year central contract in October only to be left out of the subsequent ODI tri-series in Pakistan and both squads for Australia.

Shunted down to England Lions duty, Ahmed impressed under new head coach Jonathan Trott on the recent trip to St Kitts to face West Indies A. He put both sides of his game together in the second unofficial ODI, scoring 108 at number three before claiming five for 60 with the ball.

He is due to join the Lions again in South Africa soon, but Jacks' withdrawal could be his chance to reconnect with the senior squad.

articles.title: Andoni Iraola demands 'complete performance' from Liverpool to ruin Mauricio Pochettino's Man Utd debut
articles.summary: Andoni Iraola has challenged his Liverpool squad to reach their maximum potential as they prepare to welcome Manchester United to Anfield. The highly anticip...
articles.body:
Andoni Iraola has challenged his Liverpool squad to reach their maximum potential as they prepare to welcome Manchester United to Anfield. The highly anticipated North West derby carries extra weight this time around with Mauricio Pochettino set to take charge of the visitors for the first time.

Iraola is fully aware of the magnitude of the task ahead as United arrive on Merseyside, with the Spaniard eager to secure a result that reflects the intensity of the rivalry. Iraola highlighted the unique nature of the fixture, noting that form often goes out the window when these two giants of the English game collide on the pitch.

Writing in the official Liverpool FC matchday programme , Iraola expressed his excitement. "The first thing to say is that it is definitely good to be back, especially with a game as big as the one we have today. I know that this is a fixture that supporters of both clubs will look forward to and it is no different for those of us who are involved as players or coaches. Liverpool versus Manchester United can only ever create a sense of anticipation, no matter when and where the game is played and no matter who is involved," the Reds boss explained.

The manager is determined to ensure his players understand the gravity of the occasion . He continued: "For us it is a privilege and it is one that comes with a lot of responsibility because of what this rivalry means. The eyes of the world will be on us and we should use this as a motivation. We want – and will almost certainly need – to be as near to our best as we can. That is the standard of this fixture."

Iraola is calling for a "complete performance" where every player is fully committed from the opening whistle. He referenced previous high-profile matches against Manchester City and Arsenal, where he felt the team lacked the final clinical edge to secure maximum points at home. For this specific derby, he insists that anything less than total concentration will likely result in a missed opportunity against a dangerous United side.

"That means being all in from the very start and in every single moment from then on. It also means making the most of each situation. If we can do this I have no doubt that our chances of getting the kind of result that our fans and ourselves want will only increase. As always, the responsibility is with us so hopefully on and off the pitch we can show the best face of Liverpool by being together from the first whistle to the last," Iraola stated.

Despite the current standings, Iraola is adamant that the gap between the two sides in the league table is irrelevant. He believes that the historical weight of the contest and the arrival of Pochettino at Old Trafford will provide United with a significant psychological boost. The Reds must be prepared for a rejuvenated opponent looking to make an immediate statement under their new leadership in one of the toughest environments in world football.

"What people think the league table tells us in this moment is not something that we can afford to be distracted by. This is a day when this kind of thing does not matter in the same way that it might otherwise. The history of the rivalry between our two clubs tells us that. We should expect and prepare for the best version of United because they will definitely see this fixture as an opportunity to start showing the best of themselves, particularly under new management," Iraola warned.

While Liverpool's away form has been exemplary, including a recent 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace, Iraola has identified their home results as an area for improvement. The Spaniard wants to see the same ruthlessness at Anfield that has served them well on their travels. He pointed out that while the atmosphere provided by the home supporters has been world-class, the players must now repay that faith with consistent dominance.

Reflecting on recent performances, he noted: "This is so important because it is very difficult to go away and win anywhere in this league, but at the same time it makes it even more vital that we start to bring our home form up to a similar standard. In some cases, small margins have made a big difference to the outcome of our home games. I say this not to make it feel better or to look for excuses, but to highlight that we have to do more to either turn some of these small margins in our favour or take them out of the equation altogether."

articles.title: Report: Colts shutting down WR Alec Pierce for 2026 season
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce reportedly won't be returning this season.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce reportedly won't be returning this season.

According to Ian Rapoport , the Colts are "planning for Alec Pierce to be fully healthy for 2027, turning away his efforts to return with a few games left this season."

Rapoport added, "Despite his attempts, Pierce's season is almost certainly over, according to sources."

This decision comes with the Colts 3-8 on the season and after the team has moved on from a number of players, including Daniel Jones, Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, and Josh Downs.

When Shane Steichen has been asked in recent weeks about Pierce's recovery and when he could potentially return, no specifics or a timeline had been given.

Pierce has spent most of the season on injured reserve, rehabbing his re-aggravated left heel, which he injured in Week 2 against Kansas City. Pierce underwent offseason surgery on the same injury.

Without Pierce to stretch the field, the Colts ' passing game has been stagnant without that vertical presence.

"The Colts' goal is to avoid a similar situation next year, which is why the team is insisting that his 2026 season is over," Rapoport wrote.

During the 2024 and 2025 seasons, Pierce has led the NFL in yards per catch. He eclipsed 1,000 receiving yards in 2025.

This offseason, Pierce signed a four-year, $114 million deal to return to the Colts in free agency.

articles.title: Houston high school football: Takeaways and top performers from area playoffs
articles.summary: From dazzling running back performances to eye-opening wins, the second round of the UIL football playoffs provided plenty to talk about.
articles.body:
From dazzling running back performances to eye-opening wins, the second round of the Texas high school football playoffs provided plenty to talk about. Here's a look at some of the key takeaways and top performers.

La Porte running back Sean Simon has been a prolific ball carrier for the Bulldogs since his freshman year. But what he accomplished on Friday night at Tomball ISD Stadium was certainly his best performance yet.

The junior four-star recruit rushed for a program-record 458 yards and seven touchdowns on 41 carries during a 63-49 win over College Station in the Class 5A Division I bracket. Six of those touchdowns came in the first half.

Simon's performance earned him two more entries in the Houston high school football record book . He now tied with several other players for second place in the single-game touchdown category. His yardage against College Station also ranks as the eighth-highest single-game total and gives him a career-high 2,547 for the season.

With 6,340 career rushing yards, Simon now ranks 13th in Houston high school football history. With his output against College Station, he passed Katy's Deondrick Glass, Pearland's Anthony Evans and Tomball's Bubba Greeley.

La Porte (10-2) will take on Angleton (11-1) in the regional semifinals at 7 p.m. Friday at Freedom field.

College Park and Klein were both on the brink of elimination Friday night. But the Cavaliers and Bearkats kept fighting and ultimately mounted late comebacks to keep their seasons alive for at least one more week.

College Park (9-3) trailed Langham Creek by two scores in the third quarter before finishing the game with 16 unanswered points to pull out a 28-21 victory in the Class 6A Division II bracket. Kaylen Stephens had a big game on the ground for the Cavaliers, rushing for 188 yards and two touchdowns on 28 carries. Antonio Booker added 91 yards on 15 carries as College Park rushed for 303 as a team and secured its second straight trip to the third round.

College Park will battle No. 1 state-ranked North Crowley (12-0) at 7 p.m. Friday at Waco ISD Stadium.

Klein (11-1), meanwhile, trailed 27-10 against The Woodlands in the third quarter before making a furious rally to win 31-27. Kendrick Brown scored the go-ahead touchdown on a 1-yard run with 1:30 remaining, sending the Bearkats to the third round of the playoffs for the first time since 2009 when the program reached the semifinals.

Klein will take on Waxahachie (11-1) at 2 p.m. Saturday at Waco ISD Stadium.

Katy continued its dominant season with a 47-7 victory in a true road game against Hutto in the Class 6A Division I bracket Friday night. The Tigers (12-0) stayed true to their M.O., rushing for 398 yards and six touchdowns while averaging 8 yards per carry. Senior Tony Manuel III was the catalyst for the ground attack with 202 yards and three touchdowns on 18 carries, and junior C.J. Watts added 85 yards and three touchdowns on 13 carries.

The defense had a strong performance as well against a Hutto team that was averaging 55.3 points per game. Senior linebacker Cade Haug and junior defensive back Braden Hugenberg each had an interception for the Tigers. Katy held a 24-0 lead at halftime and did not allow the Hippos to get on the scoreboard until the fourth quarter. Katy is allowing just 10.1 points per game this season and has limited six of its last seven opponents to single digits.

The Tigers will take on Summer Creek (8-4) in the regional semifinals at 2 p.m. Friday at Turner Stadium. It's a rematch from a game they lost 38-37 in the same round last year on a last-minute touchdown drive by the Bulldogs.

The second-round matchup between C.E. King and Shadow Creek in the Class 6A Division II bracket had all the makings of a game that could be competitive … at least on paper. Both teams finished the regular season as top-10 state-ranked teams, and they had just two losses between them. But the actual game was anything but competitive as C.E. King took control right out of the gates and rolled to a 62-18 victory to reach the regional semifinals.

C.E. King (11-1), which has now won 10 consecutive games, jumped out to a 28-6 lead by the end of the first quarter and never took its foot off the gas. Leading 42-18 at the end of the third quarter, the Panthers outscored the Sharks 20-0 in the final period and denied them the chance to reach the third round for the first time since 2000.

C.E. King was dominant with its rushing attack, piling up 326 yards and eight touchdowns at 8.6 yards per carry. Quarterback Khylan Davis rushed for 81 yards and touchdown and passed for 117 and another score. Receiver Dillon Mitchell collected 204 all-purpose yards, including 73 rushing and 71 receiving. Running backs Tristian Willis, Antwon Sanders and Tyrin Gatson each scored a pair of touchdowns to help lead the ground game.

C.E. King will take on Ridge Point (12-0) at 2 p.m. Saturday at Pridgeon Stadium.

Ethan Meadows, RB, Tompkins: Another playoff game, another massive performance for Meadows. The senior rushed for 341 yards and five touchdowns during the Falcons' 45-28 victory against Waller in the Class 6A Division II bracket. Meadows averaged 13.6 yards per carry and now has more than 2,000 yards for the season. He has rushed for 572 yards and seven touchdowns in two playoff games for Tompkins (9-3), which has reached the third round of the playoffs for just the fourth time in program history and for the first time since 2021.

Ja'Voris Taylor, QB, North Shore: Taylor was lights-out during the Mustangs' 52-14 victory against Pearland in the Class 6A Division I bracket. The senior completed 17-of-21 passes (81%) for 375 yards and three touchdowns. Michael Camacho Jr. had five catches for 164 yards and two touchdowns, and La'Damian Defreeze had five catches for 168 yards and a touchdown for a North Shore (11-1) passing attack that finished with 437 total yards.

Devyn Evans, DB, Angleton: Evans had 10 tackles and two interceptions for the Wildcats' defense, which put together yet another strong performance in the Class 5A Division I bracket. Caden Scott had a team-high 12 tackles, an interception and a blocked kick for Angleton, which has limited nine of its 11 opponents to 14 points or less. After losing in the bi-district round last year, the Wildcats (11-1) have returned to the regional semifinals.

Keldrid Ben, RB, Montgomery: Ben had another standout game for the Bears, helping them to 62-28 win over Pflugerville in the Class 5A Division II bracket. Ben rushed for 145 yards and four touchdowns on 14 carries, and teammate Josh Warren added a team-high 177 yards and a touchdown on 14 carries. Their contributions helped Montgomery (12-0) rush for 354 yards as a team and advance to the third round for the first time since 2010.

Alvin Mosley, WR, Crawford: Mosley hit a significant career milestone while helping Crawford to a 45-0 win over Texas City in the Class 5A Division II bracket. The Ole Miss commit had eight catches for 123 yards and three touchdowns, giving him 3,104 career receiving yards. He is just the 11th player in Houston high school football history to clear 3,000 and now ranks ninth in that category, right ahead of former North Shore standouts Quanell Farrakhan Jr. and Shadrach Banks. With 47 career touchdown catches, Mosley ranks third all-time in the city's history behind CeeDee Lamb (48) and Jermaine Bishop Jr. (55). Mosley, who also had a 40-yard rushing touchdown against Texas City, will lead the Chargers (11-1) against Huntsville at noon on Saturday at Legacy Stadium.

Kash Schwab, RB, Bridgeland: Schwab had a huge game for the Bears during their 45-0 victory against Jordan on Saturday afternoon, rushing for 275 yards and five touchdowns on 26 carries. His contributions helped Bridgeland (11-1) rush for 481 yards as a team and advance to the regional semifinals for the second time in three years.

articles.body:
Max Verstappen said George Russell is "so far below my level" after winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix, and called Russell's late mistake karma.

The two clashed at Turn 14 in final practice on Friday, Nov. 20, and the stewards gave Verstappen a warning for erratic driving. Asked about it in the FIA press conference after qualifying, Verstappen said only, "Nothing happened." Russell went further, telling Sky Sports Italy that Verstappen does it "week in, week out with many drivers" and that "somebody's got to stand up to that guy."

There was no drama on Lap 1 of the race on Saturday night, when they started side by side on the front row. They swapped the lead several times, and their race-long battle never got dangerous. With Andrea Kimi Antonelli in the mix toward the end, it ended badly for Russell.

Running third behind Verstappen and his Mercedes teammate Antonelli, Russell tried to retake second into Turn 5 three laps from the end. He ran off line and over debris, seemingly from Isack Hadjar's car, locked up and went head-on into the barrier, according to F1 . He rejoined and finished ninth . "I could have been conservative and I would probably have come home P3," Russell said.

In the FIA press conference after the race, Verstappen was asked whether Russell's comments had been on his mind and whether it was nice to get one up on him.

"Well, I mean, it's not like it's like a success today," said Verstappen. "I mean, the thing is, he speaks a lot next to the track. And honestly, for me, it doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that, so it doesn't bother me.

"And today karma is a b**ch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror, and I saw what was happening. So, I was like, 'fantastic, my day is only getting better'. And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete."

Verstappen didn't spell out what he saw in his mirror, but he was leading when Russell went off at Turn 5.

Verstappen Pulls Away in the Fight for Second

The win, Verstappen's fourth of the season, took him to 304 points, second in the drivers' standings behind champion Antonelli. Lewis Hamilton is third on 267, and Russell and Lando Norris are tied on 264, so Verstappen heads into the last two races, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, 40 points clear of Russell in the fight to finish runner-up.

The race had 35 lead changes, and the first question Verstappen got in the press conference was when he had last won a race like it.

"I probably shouldn't say it, I probably should not," said Verstappen. "I remember winning one like this when I was playing Mario Kart. Yeah, sometimes you drop back, and you get drafts, and there's like a catch-up. Always when you're dropping back, you go faster. So that's the last time that I felt something like this."

articles.title: 'I fulfilled a dream!' - Leandro Paredes reacts to winning silverware as Juan Roman Riquelme lands first title as Boca Juniors president
articles.summary: Leandro Paredes celebrated a dream fulfilled as Boca Juniors beat Atletico Mineiro 2-0 to win a record third Copa Sudamericana title and hand Juan Roman Riqu...
articles.body:
Leandro Paredes celebrated a dream fulfilled as Boca Juniors beat Atletico Mineiro 2-0 to win a record third Copa Sudamericana title and hand Juan Roman Riquelme his first international trophy as president. Their triumph in Barranquilla ended an 18-year continental wait for the club.

Paredes celebrates as Riquelme claims first title

Boca Juniors defeated Atletico Mineiro 2-0 at the Estadio Metropolitano Roberto Melendez in Barranquilla to become the first three-time Copa Sudamericana champions. Santiago Ascacibar opened the scoring in the 16th minute before Miguel Merentiel struck three minutes into the second half.

The victory ended Boca's 18-year wait for an international trophy since the 2008 Recopa and gave club president Juan Roman Riquelme his first continental crown as an executive. Having won three Copa Libertadores titles in Boca's number 10 shirt as a player, Riquelme now shares continental silverware with the Xeneize from the directors' box.

Paredes hails dream title after returning home

Leandro Paredes captained and drove Boca's campaign after returning to the club, leading CONMEBOL competitions in 2026 with 791 completed passes, 234 final-third passes and 212 line-breaking passes. Speaking to ESPN after the final whistle, Paredes shared his emotion at winning silverware back in Azul y Oro .

"I fulfilled a dream," Paredes said. "I always dreamed of being able to win a title. I only have words of gratitude for the club. Thanks to my children, my family and my friends. Since I was little, I've been taught to compete and win everything possible. I love winning and competing. I'm lucky to achieve important things."

Riquelme's mid-year reset and Villa's impact

After finishing third in Copa Libertadores Group D, Boca pivoted in June under Riquelme's leadership by appointing former team-mate Rodolfo Arruabarrena as head coach and bringing in players including Sebastian Villa, who assisted Merentiel's second-half goal in Barranquilla. Back in March at the CONMEBOL group draw, Riquelme had already spoken of the pull of continental football , saying: "Playing in the Copa always creates excitement, both in the squad and among our fans."

Villa also highlighted his joy after helping Boca past O'Higgins, Deportivo Recoleta, Sao Paulo and Vasco da Gama on the way to the final. "I'm very happy, thank God it happened, returning to the club that gave me the opportunity," Villa told ESPN. "I came back with great enthusiasm and a desire for a title. I've won two in a row."

Libertadores return and Recopa await in 2027

Lifting the Copa Sudamericana brings a USD 10,000,000 champions' prize and direct entry into the 2027 Copa Libertadores group stage without qualifying rounds. Boca also earn a berth in the 2027 Recopa against the winner of the November 28 Libertadores final between Palmeiras and Estudiantes de La Plata.

With the Argentine Cup and domestic league still ahead alongside Villa's recent local title success, Riquelme and Paredes have set the stage for another busy campaign.

articles.title: Watford sack boss Dionisi after 18 games
articles.summary: Watford sack head coach Alessio Dionisi after 18 games in charge.
articles.body:
Watford are looking for their sixth manager in 18 months after they sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following 18 games in charge.

The 46-year-old Italian was appointed in June after the departure of Ed Still, who himself lasted only three months at Vicarage Road.

Still, Javi Gracia and Paulo Pezzolano were all also given full-time contracts after Tom Cleverley left in May 2025.

Dionisi was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, and leaves the Hornets searching for a 25th since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.

The club have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history.

The decision to replace him comes after Saturday's crushing 4-0 defeat by Sheffield United at Bramall Lane.

Dionisi's dismissal caps an underwhelming start to the season, with the Hornets having won just four league games to leave them 21st in the table.

"We thank Alessio and his staff for his professionalism and their efforts," sporting director Luke Dowling told the club website.

"As I'm sure the supporters have seen, Alessio is a really good guy and we wish him the best for the future.

"The process has started for a replacement and we hope to be in a position to announce that shortly."

Dionisi was sacked by Serie B club Empoli in March after only five months in charge following a run of five wins in 22 matches.

His spell in charge of the Hornets was his first outside his homeland and started promisingly when his youthful side beat Southampton in their opening league game.

But they won only two of their next 12 in all competitions, and despite deservedly beating Charlton on 17 October, reverses at Wolves and Norwich followed, before four points from Dionisi's final three games in charge of the Hertfordshire side and his dismissal means further upheaval for the Hornets.

Since sacking Cleverley at the end of the 2024-25 campaign, the club has now been through four permanent head coaches, as well as interim boss Charlie Daniels' two-game spell in charge.

Of those four, only Gracia, in his second spell at Vicarage Road, took charge of more than 20 games.

On the morning of their final-day drubbing by Coventry last season, chief executive Scott Duxbury wrote a statement on the club website saying Watford had made mistakes, labelling their end to the campaign "unacceptable" and "truly disappointing in the extreme".

articles.title: Ranking Montreal Screwjob and the 10 Greatest Moments in WWE Survivor Series History
articles.summary: Survivor Series has been a staple of the WWE calendar since its inception in 1987 and in the 40 years since that first show in Richfield, Ohio, the premium live event has been responsible for some of the most unforgettable, influential, and historically significant moments in professional wrestling history.
articles.body:
Survivor Series has been a staple of the WWE calendar since its inception in 1987 and in the 40 years since that first show in Richfield, Ohio, the premium live event has been responsible for some of the most unforgettable, influential, and historically significant moments in professional wrestling history.

Find out in this countdown, which takes us from the heartland of the United States on Thanksgiving night to the cold, bitter reality of Montreal.

One year after debuting at the same event, The Undertaker stalked toward the ring to challenge Hulk Hogan for the WWE Championship in Detroit, Michigan, at the 1991 Survivor Series.

He did so at a time when Hulkamania was losing its grasp on the WWE Universe. Fans had grown tired of saying prayers, eating vitamins, and working out, and they wanted change.

They got it that Thanksgiving night, courtesy of The Phenom tombstoning The Hulkster onto a steel chair, placed in the ring by the interfering " Real World's Champ " Ric Flair, and covering him for the win and the title.

It was a monumental night for The Undertaker, whose meteoric rise could be attributed to Mark Calaway's commitment to the character and a fan base that demanded more than the tired sameness that had dominated WWE airwaves for nearly a decade.

The cheers for Undertaker as he pinned Hogan ensured Hulkamania would never run quite as wild as it did before and that the Deadman was the star of the future in WWE.

The Invasion storyline pitting WWE vs. WCW was a colossal disappointment, thanks to the lack of the iconic stars from the latter and Vince McMahon's noncommittal creative when it came to booking those competitors who did make the jump as true equals to his Superstars.

What should have been an industry-changing program instead limped into the 2001 event, ready to be put out of its misery so the business could move on from the remnants of Ted Turner's wrestling promotion.

How does something so gloomy make this list, you might wonder?

The Winner Takes All showdown between Team WWE and Team Alliance (WCW and ECW) is, arguably, the greatest traditional Survivor Series match-up in the show's four-decade history.

A star-studded affair that featured The Rock, Chris Jericho, Undertaker, Kane, and Big Show battling "Stone Cold" Steve Austin, Kurt Angle, Booker T, Rob Van Dam, and Shane McMahon, it thrived on the larger-than-life stars and benefited from a red-hot crowd.

WWE won, predictably, when Angle betrayed his team, but the fans were along with the Superstars on the roller coaster ride and the result was a brilliant bit of business that proved the five-on-five format still worked.

8. Goldberg Squashes Brock Lesnar (2016)

Goldberg returned to WWE in 2016 for a titanic battle with Brock Lesnar in what was the resumption of a rivalry last seen on the company's television 12 years earlier.

The Beast had returned in 2012 and wreaked havoc on the company, beating everyone in his path and destroying everything around him, including the Undertaker's unbeaten streak at WrestleMania 30.

Goldberg was the last chance WWE had to stop The Conqueror or, at least, halt his momentum.

Goldberg steamrolled Lesnar, shocking the wrestling world by beating the Beast in under two minutes. He speared and jackhammered his way to victory, earning a huge win in his return match and setting up a story in which he was the only Superstar to have Lesnar's number.

It would culminate six months later at WrestleMania with Lesnar finally getting his win, but the stunning unpredictability of Goldberg squashing Lesnar in a high-profile main event like that was undeniable and earned the entire ordeal its place on this list.

Expectations for The Rock at Survivor Series ⭐

Booking Moves WWE Must Make to Save SmackDown 🙏

One of WWE's most barbaric matches debuted in the main event of the 2002 show as Triple H defended the World Heavyweight Championship against Shawn Michaels, Chris Jericho, Kane, Booker T, and Rob Van Dam inside the Elimination Chamber.

An unforgiving structure made of steel and chain wrecked the bodies of all involved, including some genuinely cringe-worthy bumps.

Triple H delivered one of his gutsiest performances in the match. The Game suffered a crushed larynx after taking one of Van Dam's knees to the throat during a Five Star Frog Splash attempt that was adversely affected by the limited space in the structure.

He would continue the match, competing for nearly 40 minutes while gasping for air.

His rivalries with RVD, Kane, and Shawn Michaels all received the spotlight, while Jericho turned in an MVP-worthy performance. Ultimately, Michaels earned the win and the title in just his second match since returning from a four-year hiatus and celebrated to end the show on a happy note.

The work put in by those six Superstars ensured the success of the match, which now has a spot on WWE's annual premium live event calendar, on a show of the same name.

For decades, Sting was the last holdout of WCW. He was the one Superstar who never made the jump to WWE, instead remaining loyal to the company that gave him a chance to be a major star in professional wrestling.

After a long stint in TNA Wrestling following the closure of Ted Turner's wrestling empire, Sting finally signed on the dotted line to join WWE and at the 2014 Survivor Series, made his debut as only he could.

With Triple H and Stephanie McMahon interfering in the closing moments of a battle for authority between their team and John Cena's squad, the cawing of a crow sounded over the arena's sound system and Sting walked through the curtain for the first time, to a thunderous ovation.

The Icon stalked to the ring, dropped Triple H with a Scorpion Death Drop, and placed Dolph Ziggler on top of Seth Rollins, ensuring the babyface would earn the win and end The Authority's tyrannical run.

It was a magical moment that had wrestling fans genuinely excited about the future, with Sting on board, and the possibility of some dream matches that had yet to come to fruition.

Unfortunately, a neck injury suffered the following September effectively ended Sting's run with the company, an outcome that does, admittedly, hurt his momentous debut's positioning on this list.

Vince Russo's magnum opus as the head of WWE Creative came at the 1998 Survivor Series, with the execution of the Deadly Game tournament to crown a new WWE champion.

Was the in-ring portion of the tournament any good? Absolutely not, but it did not have to be. Instead, it was a tournament that featured several intertwining and ongoing stories that wrote new chapters, settled others, saw Shane McMahon reveal an alliance with his evil father, Vince, by screwing over "Stone Cold" Steve Austin, and set up a finale between The Rock and Mankind.

In the weeks leading up to the show, the scheming Mr. McMahon had manipulated Mankind into becoming his "corporate" champion, a hand-picked titleholder he knew he could control.

Meanwhile, The Rock's popularity was through the roof, thanks to a crowd that appreciated his entertainment value and his big-time match performances, such as his Ladder Match against Triple H at SummerSlam 1998.

Imagine the surprise of the fans, then, when Rock trapped Mankind in a Sharpshoter, raised the People's Eyebrow, and watched as McMahon called for the bell.

The fix was in. Rock embraced both McMahons, revealing himself to be the real Corporate Champion while Mankind was little more than a pawn in McMahon's chess game.

The manner in which The Corporation's screw jobs of Austin and Mankind came to fruition, The Rock conveniently found ways to win, and all of the moving pieces fit seamlessly, resulted in one of the great one-night tournament shows in pro wrestling history, at the height of the company's popularity.

"Million Dollar Man" Ted DiBiase promised a mystery partner for his team at the 1990 event and what he delivered would change WWE forever.

The future Hall of Famer introduced the fans in the Hartford Civic Center to "Kane The Undertaker," which was eventually shortened to "The Undertaker," and the rest was history.

The man who would go on to win four WWE titles, three world heavyweight titles, go 21-0 at WrestleMania in his first 21 matches, become the most loyal Superstar of them all, and a workhorse for Vince McMahon's company, stalked to the ring amid silence from the fans, many of whom did not know how to react to the mesmerizing newcomer.

In short order, he dispatched the opposition, eliminating future Hall of Famers Koko B. Ware and Dusty Rhodes, before being counted out amid his continued dominance.

The outcome did not matter. What did matter was the first impression he left on fans.

As you already know, he would channel his performance into a WWE title match within a year, a sign of approval from management, following the reception for the character by fans, all of which can be contributed to Mark Calaway taking a persona that should have failed and making the absolute most of it.

The idea of CM Punk returning to WWE following a well-documented walk-out in 2013 and subsequent comments (and lawsuits) made about the promotion seemed beyond far-fetched.

Add to that a less-than-graceful divorce from AEW following backstage fights with his fellow talent, and it seemed like there was no chance in hell that Punk would be welcomed back in WWE with open arms.

Mended fences and reconstructed bridges between both sides, though, made it a possibility.

In November of 2023, just as it appeared that the Survivor Series would go off the air with Cody Rhodes, Sami Zayn, Jey Uso, Randy Orton, and Seth Rollins celebrating their win over The Judgment Day, "Cult of Personality" played and Punk stepped through the curtain to a deafening pop.

Fans jumped up and down, some with tears in their eyes, as the hometown hero returned in Chicago and to a fan base eager to have him back.

Some of his fellow Superstars? Not so much, including Rollins, whose tantrum has been well-documented.

It was one of the highly controversial, yet unforgettable moments that Survivor Series had long been associated with, and it helped continue a period for Triple H as the Chief Content Officer of WWE in which he continued to build momentum.

As the villainous CM Punk defended his WWE Championship against Ryback and John Cena in a Triple Threat Match in the closing moments of the 2013 Survivor Series, The Shield made a debut that would have generational implications on the WWE product.

Roman Reigns, Dean Ambrose, and Seth Rollins hopped the guardrail and took down Ryback with a triple powerbomb through the announce table, eliminating the unstoppable force and making it possible for the battered Punk to retain his title.

Few could have known at the time the impact of the moment.

The arrival of those three NXT standouts would shape the next decade-plus in WWE (and beyond). Reigns, Ambrose, and Rollins would dominate both as The Shield and in singles competition.

All three captured world titles, main-evented significant pay-per-view events, and became centerpieces of the company's creative, marketing, and promotional efforts.

Reigns became the biggest star of his generation, Rollins is among the most popular and respected in-ring performers of his era, and Ambrose carried a huge fan following that he took with him when he decided to join All Elite Wrestling in 2019, where he remains its biggest star.

So much of what we fondly remember over the last 14 years involves one of the three of those Superstars, whose paths in WWE may have been drastically different if they had not captured the attention and imagination of the fans as The Shield on that first night and in every subsequent performance thereafter.

When someone says "Survivor Series," one moment has become synonymous with the event: the Montreal Screwjob.

In 1997, Bret Hart was one his way out of WWE and, given creative control through the end of his run by Vince McMahon as part of the negotiations for his exit, The Hitman refused to drop the company's top prize to Shawn Michaels in his home country of Canada.

He offered to lose it to Steve Austin, The Undertaker, Ken Shamrock, even the Brooklyn Brawler. He promised to lose it at another time, in the United States, but he had worked too hard on his pro-Canada character to lose the title there, especially to a performer he did not believe respected him.

All of that was captured in the 1998 documentary, Hitman Hart: Wrestling With Shadows , as well as recorded conversations between Hart and Vince McMahon over how to handle the finish of the match.

A schmozz was agreed upon that would see Triple H interfere on Michaels' behalf, and British Bulldog, Jim Neidhart, and Owen Hart interfere to help Hart, just after HBK trapped the Hitman in his own finishing move.

The match went according to plan until McMahon made an unscheduled and highly suspicious appearance at ringside. When Michaels trapped Hart in the Sharpshooter, McMahon demanded the bell be rung and the title awarded to the challenger.

Wrestling fans had witnessed the most blatant and unapologetic screwjob in pro wrestling history play out in front of their very eyes. Hart, infuriated, destroyed monitors, cameras, and tables around ringside, spat in his boss' face, and wrote "WCW" with his finger in the air.

It was a chaotic moment the likes of which we have never seen before, probably will never see again, and remains one of the darkest days in pro wrestling history.

No matter what comes of a Survivor Series premium live event from here on out, nothing will have the impact or historical significance of that night north of the border, when wrestling as we knew it changed forever.

articles.title: Jose The Best, limpiacristales de profesión y showman de pádel por accidente
articles.standfirst: Este madrileño se ha ganado el cariño del mundo del pádel por haber hecho de su trabajo todo un espectáculo que da la vuelta al mundo.
articles.summary: Este madrileño se ha ganado el cariño del mundo del pádel por haber hecho de su trabajo todo un espectáculo que da la vuelta al mundo.
articles.body: No todas las estrellas en el pádel llevan pala. El universo del 20x10 es cada vez más variado y entre tanto astro hay una figura exótica, ajena, que sin buscarlo se ha colado para brillar con personalidad propia en la pista empuñando una rasqueta y un hisopo y que cuenta con el amor incondicional del aficionado. Porque si te digo José Fernández Ruiz (Madrid, España, 1981) puede que creas que estoy hablándote de tu vecino. O quizá de uno más de los casi 500.000 Joses, Pepes, Joselitos o Pepines que existen en España. Incluso puede que creas que lo hago de otro Fernández más de esos que son muy amables como decía el anuncio, y que contamos casi por un millón en nuestro país. Pero no es así. Y lo sabrás porque si te digo Jose 'The Best' quizá ahí la cosa ya cambie. Y es que es este apodo la seña de identidad que le identifica. 'The Best' es el pseudónimo con el que un madrileño que empezó su vida laboral en el pádel de rebote se ha ganado el cariño y admiración de toda una industria por su trabajo, con algo tan básico como la limpieza de los cristales de la pista, pero habiéndole dado una vuelta para convertirlo en todo un show. “Yo soy un tío que limpia pistas. Jose Fernández es tímido, un tipo normal y cuando soy 'The Best' me transformo, me gusta divertirme con la gente y pasármelo bien. Creo que esa es la clave de que todo fluya y el público disfrute”, explica a MARCA con naturalidad una de las figuras que mayor explosión social y mediática ha vivido en los últimos años. A pesar de su reciente boom lleva en el pádel muchos años, más a la sombra que bajo el foco, por cierto, porque cuando este deporte no era mainstream y apenas estaba empezando a explotar Jose ya había empezado a trabajar en eventos de pádel para ofrecer un servicio que pasa tan desapercibido que es indispensable. “Soy un tío de barrio, alguien normal, que empezó su vida profesional siendo militar y que, al dejarlo, trabajaba en una empresa de limpieza y nos llegó un cliente de pádel en 2012 o 2013. Tuve suerte, caí en gracia y, creo, que me ha ido bien porque siempre he sido muy respetuoso y profesional con mi trabajo”, continúa detallando sus inicios. Pero, cómo se da el salto de ser un trabajador más, otro operario de esos que trabaja en el backstage de la industria que no vemos y que ajeno al brilli brilli hace su labor con dignidad y profesionalismo. Dónde estuvo la clave para tener nombre, apellidos, apodo y hasta marcas que le patrocinan. “Empecé como asalariado y estuve 4 o 5 años trabajando en World Padel Tour a través de mi empresa. Entonces se limpiaba la pista solo una vez al día. Estuve un año sin saber nada del pádel y a partir de ahí recibí la llamada de Premier Padel. Aguanté un par de años compaginándolo con mi otro trabajo, pero llegó un momento hace como dos años en el que tuve que elegir porque no tenía vida personal”, confiesa ahora que se dedicar íntegramente a su show, Jose 'The Best' limpiacristales. Un cambio que no ha sido radical, de esos que cambian vidas, sino que se ha ido gestando paulatinamente y que le ha llevado a compaginar diferentes trabajos, viajes sin dormir y muchas horas lejos de casa dentro de una pista de pádel o al volante de un coche. “Todo cambió en un torneo en Jaén. Después de limpiar la pista salí del evento y la gente me pedía fotos y para mí no era normal. Ahí decidí abrirme una cuenta en Instagram y en menos de una semana ya tenía miles de seguidores”, recuerda mientras se le escapa una media sonrisa del que vivió algo tan inesperado como reconfortante. Porque aunque la fama le llegó, el trabajo se resistía y tuvo que salir a buscarlo. Las redes sociales fueron el escaparate de alguien que tuvo que trabajarse la confianza de promotores, jugadores, marcas y afición para acabar teniendo premio. “Empezó de forma casual, la verdad. Tenía que estar 12 horas trabajando y me dije, vamos a probar a hacer algo diferente (se ríe). Mi idea era que las jornadas en el pádel eran largas y que quizá podía funcionar que de repente entrara un tío calvo y con barba a limpiar y hacer unos bailes”, explica de una idea que pocos se hubiera atrevido a llevar a cabo. “Cuando empecé no tenía barba y vestía con ropa de trabajo. Fue cambiando a medida que había más demanda y llegaban los promotores, los sponsors… A día de hoy tengo total libertad y me gusta salir con calcetines de colores, hacer mis bailes…”, continúa riéndose de sí mismo en un reconfortante ejercicio de no tomarse demasiado en serio alguien que, aunque prefiera no contarlo en público, los que conocemos su historia no olvidamos cómo fue tratado en el final de su etapa en WPT porque generaba envidias que le fuera bien. Así que sí, la historia de Jose es la de alguien que hizo de la necesidad, oportunidad. Lejos de romantizar su evolución este madrileño se agarró a una idea loca para construir un show que acompaña de mucha habilidad rasqueta en mano, coreografías, actuaciones en pista y activaciones con un publico que se entrega a su momento. Madrileño y de barrio, asturiano de corazón y más de escapadas al pueblo que de vuelos largos al paraíso, no quiere normalizar que lo suyo sea algo más que solo trabajo. “A ver, que me dedico a limpiar cristales no a operar a corazón abierto (se ríe). La idea siempre ha sido la misma, tomarme como algo muy importante mi trabajo, ser profesional y pasármelo bien”, continúa explicando que empezó siendo el responsable de personal en la limpieza cuando hablaba más de bolsas de basura, baños o ceniceros que de ser o no una celebrity y hacerse fotos con la star system. Pero, sí, lo es. No juega al pádel porque se le da “muy, muy mal”, pero es el mejor en lo suyo y se ha ganado el amor de la gente, primero, y “poder vivir de esto que, aunque no da para un sueldo Nescafé, sí me permite ser feliz”, después. En ese orden, sí, y no es poco porque a pesar de la exposición su figura no genera crítica, hate o duda alguna. “A mi me encanta que la gente me pida fotos o un autógrafo. Si yo tengo trabajo es por el público y porque el show que hago les gusta. Me debo a la gente y si, por ejemplo, hay 10 personas que me piden fotos al acabar el día jamás me iría al hotel sin atender a todos”, describe de algo que ya se ha convertido en rutina en cada evento que pisa. Una vida que le ha llevado a vivir más de medio año lejos de casa, pero que sigue disfrutando en cada parada como si fuera la última. “Este año llevo unos 25 eventos entre Premier, PPL y Reserve. Ah, y con los eventos de padel amateur que son alucinantes porque la gente los disfruta diferente”, enumera de su 2026 mientras confiesa, al ser preguntado si no le desgasta, que “cuando entro en la pista intento olvidarme de todo porque la gente no tiene por qué ser partícipe de mis penas y sí de mis alegrías”. Quizá haya sido esa rara normalidad la que ha calado en el fan. Cualquiera que haya visitado un evento profesional de pádel sabe que Jose es un reclamo de dimensiones incalculables y que es reconocido y reconocible allá por donde va. Que si te paras a charlar con él, lo normal es que la conversación se interrumpa varias veces por aficionados que quieren una foto, simplemente felicitarle o invitarle a “una cervecita”. Pero no le ha cambiado. Sigue chapurreando el inglés, se atreve con el italiano o el francés y, si no, siempre le quedan las señas y esa sonrisa que nunca pierde. “A veces tengo el síndrome del impostor, creo que no me he ganado lo que tengo y me tengo que decir a mí mismo: creetelo”, confiesa con algo de vulnerabilidad y esa sencillez que delatan los ojos vidriosos. Se lo ha ganado y su figura ya es tan reconocida que incluso trasciende el pádel y empieza a tener que hacer malabares, como hace en pista, pero en su realidad cotidiana. “Sí, me está pasando desde hace poco que me conocen fuera del entorno pádel. Por lo visto la gente cuando voy vestido de calle también me reconoce (se ríe). El otro día estaba cenando por Madrid y me paró una pareja para pedirme una foto y tuve que mirar alrededor para ver si era a mí o me estaba equivocando”, comparte riéndose a carcajadas con esa incredulidad del que no acaba de entender ciertas situaciones que ha llegado a vivir y que busca normalizar a través del humor. Ahora que vive su momento, que está en la cresta de la ola, Jose ya empieza a preparar el mañana porque cuando se ha pasado hambre el que es vivo, y él lo es, tiene colmillo para no volver donde muchos se quedan. “La idea es que a través de mi nombre y mi trabajo, cuando el cuerpo no aguante, pueda montar una empresa para que mi sucesor o sucesora tenga mi metodología, nuestro show propio y crezcamos”, detalla de un futuro que no ve muy lejano. Y es verdad, su trabajo conlleva una serie de riesgos que, aunque no se vean, están ahí. Él ya ha vivido episodios duros como cuando “el año pasado en Rotterdam me rompí la muñeca tras caerme de una escalera a más de 3 metros y me tuvieron que meter 8 tornillos y una placa”, recuerda para acabar confesando, como es normal, que “es uno de mis grandes miedos porque si me pasa algo, todo se acaba”. Su labor “es muy exigente físicamente porque estás muchas horas preparado, pasas de estar en parado a tener que entrar rápido en pista y hacer un despliegue grande en apenas un minuto”, explica siendo consciente que “desde fuera puede parecer muy banal, pero me acuerdo que en el torneo de Madrid este año estaba calentando y desde la grada un chico le decía a su pareja, ¿pero que calienta y todo?”, continúa con gracia. Ahí radica, quizá, el ingrediente invisible que hace que su fórmula funcione. Jose Fernández sigue viviéndolo todo con esa normalidad que comentaba al principio de la entrevista sabiendo que 'The Best' le ha ayudado a vivir de algo que ni hubiera imaginado. “Me preocupa poco cómo acabe esto, pero oye, si alguien me recuerda como el que lo empezó estará genial. Al final limpiar cristales en el pádel se ha hecho y se va a hacer siempre, pero sería bonito si alguien se acuerda así de mí y que puse mi granito”, finaliza. No hay mejor forma de acabar una historia que seguro tendrá todavía mucho recorrido y que habla tanto de vida como de deporte. El suyo es el relato de alguien que tuvo suerte y se la trabajó, pero que adquiere valor porque, honestamente, tanta normalidad es un golpe de realidad ajeno a quien le va bien. Y, además, porque nos ayuda a relativizar el éxito, la fama y los seguidores recordándonos que esto al final va de que la buena gente se pueda ganar la vida con honradez, dignidad y, si puede ser, siendo felices con lo que hacen. Sean deportistas, limpiacristales, periodistas o lo que cada uno pueda o elija ser.
