articles.title: Liu Wenwei: Chinese snooker player suspended amid match-fixing investigation
articles.summary: Chinese snooker player Liu Wenwei is suspended from "attending or competing on the World Snooker Tour with immediate effect" amid an investigation into match-fixing.
articles.body:
Chinese snooker player Liu Wenwei has been suspended from "attending or competing on the World Snooker Tour with immediate effect" amid an investigation into match-fixing.

The decision was announced on Sunday by World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association (WPBSA) chairman Jason Ferguson.

"This follows an investigation into him being a party to approaches made to players to fix matches and failing to report approaches made to him to fix matches on the World Snooker Tour," said a WPBSA statement. , external

"At this stage, the investigation has not identified that any matches were fixed in this case.

"The suspension will remain in place until the conclusion of the investigation or any subsequent charges that may or may not be brought."

The 22-year-old Liu, who earned a two-year card on the World Snooker Tour starting with the 2025-26 season, has the right to appeal the decision.

Snooker increased its monitoring of match-fixing after their most high-profile case in 2023 led to 10 bans.

In an unrelated case to Liu, Liang Wenbo and Li Hang were given lifetime bans and eight others - including major winners Yan Bingtao and Zhao Xintong - were handed suspensions in 2023.

The allegations against the 10 players included manipulating games, approaching players to cheat, betting on snooker and fixing matches in 2022.

The cheating mainly revolved around fixing the scores, or the number of frames won in matches, with nine of the 10 players based in Sheffield.

WPBSA rules state that when it comes to approaches to fix matches, they should be reported "as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event not later than 24 hours after any such approach being made".

The rules add: "Further, the reporting member shall provide the WPBSA (via the Company Secretary or a Tournament Official) with all information in his or her knowledge relating to the approach and shall co-operate in any subsequent investigation and/or other action(s) arising out of such a report."

articles.title: Connor Bedard to Undergo Surgery, Latest on Blackhawks Star's Shoulder Injury and Timeline to Return
articles.summary: Chicago Blackhawks general manager Kyle Davidson announced that captain Connor Bedard will undergo shoulder surgery, according to Ben Pope of the Chicago Sun-Times.
articles.body:
Chicago Blackhawks general manager Kyle Davidson announced that captain Connor Bedard will undergo shoulder surgery, according to Ben Pope of the Chicago Sun-Times .

The procedure will happen "this week" and a return timeline will be determined following the surgery, per Pope . The Blackhawks placed Bedard on injured reserve on Sunday, retroactive to Nov. 17.

Bedard suffered the right shoulder injury during Chicago's 6-3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs on Tuesday.

The 21-year-old has dealt with health woes as of late, previously missing 12 games due to a right shoulder injury during the 2025-26 season.

Although he didn't need surgery at the time, he eventually underwent a procedure on his left shoulder due to an injury that occurred while he was training over the offseason.

Bedard was forced to miss Chicago's first six games this season as he recovered.

He eventually returned to appear in 15 contests, recording seven goals and 11 assists.

Bedard has been a key contributor for the Blackhawks throughout his career, as the 2024 Calder Memorial Trophy winner is coming off a 2025-26 campaign in which he amassed a career-high 75 points despite being limited to 69 games played.

His latest absence is a tough blow to a Chicago squad that has only compiled a 7-14-2 record to start this season.

Anton Frondell and Frank Nazar should continue to see more playing time until Bedard is able to return, although Frondell left the Blackhawks' 4-3 win over the Calgary Flames with an injury of his own on Saturday.

articles.title: ‘I am not here to defend anything’: Gukesh warns Javokhir Sindarov ahead of World Chess Championship
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Defending world champion Dommaraju Gukesh has brushed aside the pressure of expectations ahead of his title clash against Uzbekistan’s Javokhir
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Defending world champion Dommaraju Gukesh has brushed aside the pressure of expectations ahead of his title clash against Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov, insisting he is approaching the 2026 World Chess Championship with the mindset of winning the crown afresh rather than protecting it.The 14-game classical contest begins on November 24 at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, Geneva, following the opening ceremony on November 22.With both players aged 20 when Game 1 gets underway, it will be the youngest World Championship match in chess history.Asked during the opening press conference whether defending a title feels heavier than chasing it for the first time, the Indian Grandmaster made his approach clear."Well, I don't think I'm here to defend anything. I'm here to win it all over again, I think. So that's the mindset I'm in," Gukesh said on Sunday.Having won the crown at 18 in Singapore, Gukesh enters Geneva as the only player on stage who has experienced a World Championship match before.Yet, he noted that having played one does not automatically make the preparation easier, as every contest brings a different rhythm and demands its own work."I think the preparation differs from match to match. Also, in 2024, I was playing a lot more than I did this year," Gukesh said, reflecting on how his second cycle compared to his first."Sometimes it just feels like hard work. When you do certain kinds of work, sometimes it feels like fun and creativity flowing around. Working with the team that I enjoy being around is one of the most important things for me. Even when the work is exhausting or stressful, you're still surrounded by people who you like being around, and that gives you a lot of strength."'I feel like the best part about this whole World Championship journey is the training'For Gukesh, that camaraderie inside his camp, led by longtime second Grzegorz Gajewski,has been the highlight of his buildup."I feel like the best part about this whole World Championship journey is the training camps," he added. "It's so much fun, so much good work, so much laughing, so many jokes. With Gajew, I share a very close personal bond, and the training camps are probably the things that I will most remember after the match."While Sindarov arrives as the higher-rated player and holds a 2-0 classical head-to-head advantage, Gukesh spent recent months deliberately cutting back on tournaments to ease the pressure on himself and sharpen his game.Even with his experience from two years ago, he stressed that past achievements carry no weight once the clock starts ticking."Compared to the last time, it feels like I'm more experienced coming into the match, but whatever has happened till now just gets erased when we sit at the table for Game 1," Gukesh remarked."It's a completely different match, completely different opponent, different place. So I'm not really thinking about other things, just giving my best for these 14 games."'Sindarov has just been in very consistent and very good form'Gukesh also spoke warmly about his challenger's consistency over the past season, while noting that preparation in the modern engine era is about finding small edges against a well-rounded opponent."Sindarov has just been in very consistent and very good form and is surely one of the very top players at the very top of his game," Gukesh noted."When you play a World Championship, it's very nice that it's just one opponent so you can put full attention on that one specific player. There's a lot of analyzing your opponent going on, though only to an extent because Sindarov is very universal. He can play any position at a decent level. It's just you sharpening your skills and understanding your opponent to a good degree."The match follows a schedule of three games followed by a rest day, with the first player to reach 7.5 points crowned champion.The total prize fund is US $2.5 million, with each player earning US $200,000 per win and the remainder split equally.READ ALSO: The year Facebook was born, Switzerland hosted its last World Chess Championship; Gukesh vs Sindarov nextIf the scores are level at 7-7 after Game 14 on December 11, tiebreaks on December 12 will decide the title.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ex-WWE Champ Jack Swagger Suffers Permanent Vision Damage After Serious Power Slap Injury
articles.summary: Jake Hager, who previously wrestled in WWE as Jack Swagger, is facing a lifelong injury after his most recent Power Slap appearance.
articles.body:
Jake Hager, who previously wrestled in WWE as Jack Swagger, is facing a lifelong injury after his most recent Power Slap appearance.

Stuart McGurk of The Guardian reported that Hager "was left with one eyeball ruptured and a retina detached" after his loss to Johnny Magna at Power Slap 23 in Texas on Sept. 17. Hager's team "stated that, after two surgeries, he retained some sight in the eye."

After Hager's loss in September, UFC president and Power Slap co-owner Dana White said the former wrestling champ suffered the "worst injury in Power Slap or UFC history." The injury was so gruesome that White said he directed the production crew not to show the replay.

Booking Moves WWE Must Make to Save SmackDown 🙏

Hager wrestled in WWE from 2006 to 2017, winning the World Heavyweight Championship once. He later performed under his real name in AEW, aligning with Chris Jericho and the Inner Circle.

After signing with Power Slap in March, Hager won his first match before losing his last two by KO and TKO.

articles.title: How Much Money Dylan Larkin Has Lost Since Leaving Red Wings amid Suspension, Trade Request Revealed
articles.summary: The cost of Dylan Larkin's trade request from the Detroit Red Wings has now hit seven figures.
articles.body:
The cost of Dylan Larkin's trade request from the Detroit Red Wings has now hit seven figures.

The Athletic's Chris Johnston noted Larkin has forfeited more than $1 million in earnings. The Red Wings announced in October he told the team he wouldn't play another game for the team, which triggered his ongoing suspension without pay.

The website Larkin Losses has since tried to provide real-time updates as the number ticks upward.

While a deal isn't imminent, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported Saturday the Red Wings have made a "slight adjustment" in their required price. They're prepared to take back "impactful young players" rather than a veteran of similar value to Larkin:

Beyond the difficulty of putting together a worthwhile trade package for the 30-year-old forward, his no-movement clause is another complicating factor.

The Detroit Free Press ' Helene St. James reported in October he'll facilitate a move to one of 10 teams: Minnesota Wild, Florida Panthers, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche.

That still excludes two-thirds of the NHL. The Athletic's Max Bultman and Pierre LeBrun reported, for example, the Montreal Canadiens "are believed to have strong interest in Larkin" but were frozen out.

Beyond giving him a lot of leverage, Larkin's contract is probably playing a role in his committed stance. As much as he's lighter in the pocketbook, he's set to earn $8.7 million annually for the next four years. That money isn't going anywhere.

Maybe there's a point where Larkin does blink and tries to repair his relationship with Detroit. That moment doesn't appear to be arriving soon.

articles.title: Embarrassed' Auston Matthews Calls Out Maple Leafs' 'Inexcusable' Play amid Brutal Losing Streak
articles.summary: Auston Matthews was not a happy camper after the Toronto Maple Leafs blew a 3-2 lead in the final five minutes of the third period against the Columbus Blue Jackets, losing 4-3 to extend their winless streak to nine games.
articles.body:
Auston Matthews was not a happy camper after the Toronto Maple Leafs blew a 3-2 lead in the final five minutes of the third period against the Columbus Blue Jackets, losing 4-3 to extend their winless streak to nine games.

"It's obviously been a really rough stretch here, but tonight, we should be embarrassed," he told reporters . "It's not fair to the people who pay for tickets to come and watch. It's inexcusable."

The Maple Leafs have posted eight regulation losses and one overtime loss in their last nine games, dropping to last place in the Atlantic Division with 19 points. Only the Blue Jackets (18 points) and Pittsburgh Penguins (16 points) have been worse in the Eastern Conference.

Matthews has done his part, with 14 goals and 19 assists across 25 games, ranking sixth in the NHL in points (33). But it hasn't been enough to change the tide of the team's recent form, with Saturday feeling like an inflection point.

"We just threw up all over ourselves pretty much and lose the game," defenseman Jake McCabe told reporters. "... It's hard to wrap your head around, that's for sure. I thought our fans were engaged all game and into it and loud. I'd be pissed off too if I were them."

articles.title: Why Steelers' DK Metcalf was ejected after skirmishes with Cooper DeJean
articles.summary: DK Metcalf headed for an early exit on Sunday after multiple run-ins with Eagles CB Cooper DeJean.
articles.body:
The Steelers ' offense got off to a sluggish start against the Eagles on Sunday, and at least some of that is owed to the struggles of DK Metcalf.

The highly-paid receiver had just one catch for two yards on four targets before a bad day worsened with an ejection in the third quarter.

Metcalf, who has had his share of on-field infractions throughout his eight-year career, received a chorus of cheers and jeers from Eagles fans as he walked back to the locker room.

Here's a look at why Metcalf's day ended early at Lincoln Financial Field.

Metcalf was ejected Sunday after receiving his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty of the game. Replay showed Metcalf appeared to poke Eagles CB Cooper DeJean in the eye after a play:

Metcalf found himself at the center of multiple skirmishes on Sunday, including this tussle with DeJean in the first half that earned him his first unsportsmanlike penalty:

Unsurprisingly, Metcalf heard plenty of noise from the pro-Eagles crowd as he walked back to the locker room:

Metcalf was involved in another on-field incident last December when he got into an altercation with a Lions fan in Detroit. While he wasn't ejected because officials didn't see it, Metcalf received a two-game suspension from the NFL.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes goes over 300 yards in Week 11 blowout
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions in Week 11
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions in Week 11 against the Arizona Cardinals before being removed from the blowout victory early in the fourth quarter. Backup quarterback Josh Fields came in to mop up.

Why it Matters: Fantasy managers certainly got their money's worth in three quarters from Mahomes. It makes sense for head coach Andy Reid to rest Mahomes with the game out of hand, as the Chiefs have a quick turnaround playing on Thanksgiving night against the Buffalo Bills in Week 12.

articles.title: New York Jets discussion: Week 11 live chat during the Los Angeles Chargers game
articles.summary: The Jets are on the road in Los Angeles, California as they take on the Los Angeles Chargers today
articles.body:
Last week the New York Jets lost their fifth straight game, getting blown out by the Buffalo Bills in the second half after being down by just four points at halftime. The loss to the Bills gave the Jets a 2-8 record on the season. Today the Jets are on the road in Los Angeles, California as they face the 1-8 Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers have dominated the Jets in recent years, winning five straight and seven of the last nine against the Jets. This year, however, the Chargers have been awful. New Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and long time Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert have not meshed. The result has been a turnover prone, ineffective Herbert who looks nothing like the Herbert we have seen for years. The Chargers offense has been bad, and the Chargers defense has been bad. Unlike the last two weeks, this is a game the Jets have a legitimate shot to win.

Kickoff is scheduled for shortly after 4 PM EST.

Stay on top of every Jets update and debate every snap with other diehard fans. Game-day discussion is smoother in the SB Nation app.

The Jets will be missing receivers Omar Cooper Jr. and Isaiah Williams today. Garrett Wilson will need to step up if the Jets want to emerge victorious. Against a bad Chargers secondary, the Geno Smith to Garrett Wilson connection should thrive. If not, there's always next week.

articles.title: Liverpool vs Man United player ratings: Two 9/10s inspire as Mauricio Pochettino endures nightmare bow
articles.summary: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United: Rio Ngumoha and Florian Wirtz starred as Mauricio Pochettino endured horror in his first game as United manager
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino endured a dismal start to his tenure at Manchester United as Liverpool ran riot in a 4-0 victory against their relegation-threatened rivals.

A whirlwind week for the former Argentina international ended in familiar disappointment for the struggling visitors, whose hopes of a new manager bounce were decisively crushed during a nightmare opening 13 minutes at Anfield.

Dominik Szoboszlai put the hosts ahead with a fierce free-kick after defender Leny Yoro was sent off for denying a goalscoring opportunity inside just eight minutes, before Florian Wirtz 's smart finish quickly put Pochettino's side further behind.

United managed to temporarily stem the tide courtesy of crucial Senne Lammens saves, last-ditch defending, and wayward finishing, but Andoni Iraola's side redoubled their efforts after the interval.

Pochettino's 10 men were frankly fortunate that Liverpool only added two more goals through Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz, such was the overwhelming nature of their dominance.

Here are how the players rated at Anfield:

Smart stop to deny Fernandes when Man United started knocking at the door in the first half, alive to the situation after not being required in the early stages. Barely got a touch after the break, until being called until action in stoppage time to deny Fernandes consolation.

His through ball for Isak was more of a hooked clearance than a calculated lofted pass, but it still caused the chaos required to get Yoro sent off. Always willing to get in the challenge. Subbed.

Defensively sound and looked comfortable enough to sometimes step into midfield, especially when United were forced into removing an attacker to sure up their defence. Smart play to deal with a Fernandes run in behind during the second half, using his pace to get goalside and draw the foul.

Dominated physically with United not having a recognised striker on the pitch. Was similarly comfortable against the challenge of Zirkzee.

Shaky to start against Mbeumo, fortunate the Cameroonian was the sacrifice after Yoro's red.

Superbly fired home from the free-kick to fully punish the Yoro blunder and always Liverpool's engine room. Had a fair few pops from range that got Lammens scrambling.

Liverpool's metronome and came up with some delightful passes as the hosts had fun at United's expense. Subbed.

Full of running and pace but struggled to figure out when to pull the trigger, which wasted the opportunities he forged himself. The third chance he missed was a real sitter - and he made an absolute mess of it. Made up for earlier misses with a nice assist for Ngumoha. Subbed.

Excellent volley to double Liverpool's lead and thrived in the space created by Liverpool's man advantage, bringing his fine international form back to his club. Signed off on a brilliant performance with a delightful assist for Munoz.

A real demon on the left, terrorising Dalot and often leaving the Portuguese defender in his dust. Excellent work to assist Wirtz and got his deserved goal to put the game to bed, becoming this fixture's youngest scorer in Premier League history. Some talent. Subbed.

Really impressive on the whole, with the only thing missing being the goal. Looking sharp, he drew the foul that got Yoro sent off and was a constant threat against United, forcing Lammens into multiple saves before the break. He should have found the net after the break as he beared down on goal after another De Ligt error, but wildly blazed wide. Still deserves his flowers. Subbed.

Victor Munoz (Barcola, 72') - 8: Did what Barcola couldn't on this glorious afternoon for Liverpool and gobbled up the chance that fell to him. Good finish.

Trey Nyoni (Mac Allister, 72') - 7: Solid cameo from the highly-rated midfielder, who got a warm welcome when he came on.

Jeremie Frimpong (Ngumoha, 78') - 6: Susceptible to the odd error but too late for any damage to be done or anyone to care. Ran for a bit.

Joe Gomez (Araujo, 85') - N/A: Still no goal.

Beaten on the goalkeeper's side for Szoboszlai's free-kick, which wasn't a good look. However, he couldn't do a huge amount for Wirtz and Ngumoha's goals, and he made a fair few saves to limit the scoreline and technically keep United in the game for a while. It could've been seven again.

Sent off inside eight minutes. Debate over whether Isak had control of the ball but no excuse for bundling into him like that. Put his side at an instant disadvantage.

First start in a year and he looked completely out of his depth. No man's land for Araujo's hook that led to Yoro's red and was very nearly guilty. Subbed.

United's best starting defender but that's not exactly high praise. Put in a flying challenge to deny Barcola a goal in the second half.

Really struggled against the pace and skill of Ngumoha, losing nearly every duel with the electrifying teenager. Not much to offer going forward.

Inconsistent in possession and often far too passive, at one point just passing it straight to Mac Allister to spark a Liverpool counter attack, from which they nearly scored. Subbed.

Similarly struggled in the double pivot as Liverpool's man advantage saw United get overrun, but had a couple flashes of brilliance - like when he tried to set Bruno Fernandes away in the second half from his defensive final third with a superb threaded pass. Subbed.

Started brightly against Kerkez but was the sacrifice when United needed another defender. Subbed early.

The only one to really test Alisson throughout, forcing the Brazilian into a smart save in the first half before nearly netting a consolation in stoppage time. Nevertheless uninspiring and lost a lot of his battles in the middle of the park.

Physically struggled against Van Dijk and Jacquet, and subbed at half-time by a natural No 9 who could maybe handle that sort of challenge.

Harry Maguire (Mbeumo, 22') - 6: United gained a semblance of control after his arrival, something they kept hold of until half-time. But things fell apart again after half-time - couldn't keep up with Ngumoha for Liverpool's third.

Joshua Zirkzee (Cunha, 46') - 5: Brought on to give United some sort of presence up top and went unnoticed. Gave the ball away for Liverpool's fourth.

Noussair Mazraoui (Dorgu, 65') - 5: Not exactly the game-changer United needed at this moment, and they conceded two minutes after his arrival.

Mason Mount (Tielemans, 65') - 6: Not much to offer with Liverpool dominating the ball.

Andrey Santos (Mainoo, 87') - N/A: Minutes.
